The 5.x fix commit 28eb8158210d41168a62ed5f9e044f754513bc37 adds StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4() to the RequestItemServlet form values before these mail, storage, and JSP reuse paths; the reviewed spans below bind the exact 5.10 checkout to the publicly fixed Request a Copy stored XSS path without relying on eval hits or generated source-sink annotations.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-31194 / GHSA-qp5m-c3m9-8q2p describes path traversal vulnerabilities in DSpace JSPUI submission upload. The exact source snapshot eca7968be7d6b9f8f5f302c9fc09f8186ed4809e is DSpace 5.10, inside the affected 5.x range fixed in 5.11. In this checkout, JSPUI resumable upload GET handling calls DoGetResumable(), which appends the request-controlled resumableIdentifier to upload.temp.dir or java.io.tmpdir, creates that directory, and checks chunk files without canonical containment. Multipart resumable POST handling in FileUploadRequest similarly builds chunkDirPath and chunkPath from tempDir plus request parameters and writes uploaded chunks when the directory exists. The normal multipart branch writes a temp file from tempDir plus the submitted filename after basename extraction, also without canonical containment. The 5.x fix commit d1dd7d23329ef055069759df15cfa200c8e32e54 adds canonical path checks for the resumable directory, resumable chunk file, and normal upload temp file; the reviewed spans below bind the exact 5.10 checkout to the publicly fixed JSPUI upload path traversal class without relying on eval hits or generated source-sink annotations.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-31195 / GHSA-8rmh-55h4-93h5 describes path traversal in DSpace Simple Archive Format package import. The exact source snapshot eca7968be7d6b9f8f5f302c9fc09f8186ed4809e is DSpace 5.10, inside the affected 5.x line fixed in 5.11. provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-2712 describes relative path traversal in Eclipse GlassFish where request paths beginning with dot-slash are not filtered before protected resource checks, allowing unauthenticated access to WEB-INF, META-INF, configuration files, or deployed application sources. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout 0159b68b362c7f4be78d1fa75aeaf2ec0b997f1d. In that checkout, StandardContextValve.preInvoke obtains the raw request path DataChunk from HttpRequest.getRequestPathMB and directly checks only literal /META-INF and /WEB-INF prefixes. A request path such as ./WEB-INF/web.xml does not match those raw-prefix predicates before path normalization, so the protected-resource notFound branch is bypassable. Fix commit 6982a7ca7e7fb9f02276dc12ab61832daf4002bd adds normalize(String) and evaluateNormalizedPathWithSinglePoint, converts the request path to a string, normalizes dot-slash, slash, dot-dot, and single-dot path elements, and then applies the restricted-resource checks to the normalized path. This binds the advisory to source-backed request path intake, incomplete canonicalization before protected directory filtering, and the WEB-INF/META-INF access control decision.

CVE-2022-23457 / GHSA-8m5h-hrqm-pxm2 describes a path traversal bypass in ESAPI DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath(String,String,File,boolean): the default implementation may incorrectly treat the tested input path as a child of the specified parent directory. In the exact vulnerable source snapshot 2e8694c6beb3bdbb2645b882eba72ce41bc63242, DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath constructs File dir from attacker-controlled input, verifies existence/type, and then checks containment with dir.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(parent.getCanonicalPath()). This is a string-prefix check, so a sibling directory whose canonical path shares the parent path prefix can satisfy the test before the method returns the canonical directory path. The fix commit a0d67b75593878b1b6e39e2acc1773b3effedb2a is titled 'Fix for GHSL-2022-008 vulnerability.' and modifies only DefaultValidator.java, replacing the string-prefix check with dir.getCanonicalFile().toPath().startsWith(parent.getCanonicalFile().toPath()), so containment is checked on path elements rather than raw strings. Release 2.3.0.0 carries the patch and its release notes describe GHSL-2022-008 as CWE-22 path traversal in ESAPI.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-24891 describes an ESAPI default antisamy-esapi.xml configuration vulnerability where the onsiteURL regular expression did not properly sanitize javascript: URLs, so Validator.getValidSafeHTML() / AntiSamy policy validation could treat unsafe hyperlink values as safe. The exact vulnerable source snapshot 2e8694c6beb3bdbb2645b882eba72ce41bc63242 contains configuration/esapi/antisamy-esapi.xml with onsiteURL value ([\w\\/\.\?=&;\#-~]+|\#(\w)+), which allows colon-range characters and does not block encoded colon forms. The public Validator API exposes getValidSafeHTML(); DefaultValidator.getValidSafeHTML() constructs an HTMLValidationRule; HTMLValidationRule resolves and loads antisamy-esapi.xml into an AntiSamy Policy and calls AntiSamy.scan(canonical, antiSamyPolicy). The fixed esapi-2.3.0.0 source at 7797bc3ebd3a3bd700817b27e2a4455a0ba61f33 changes the onsiteURL regex to ^(?!//)(?![...]*(&colon))[...]*, and the 2.3.0.0 release notes explicitly instruct users to replace the vulnerable onsiteURL line because the old default configuration did not properly sanitize javascript: URLs.

This is review-entry retrieval ground truth only and does not claim dynamic exploit proof.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2021-4178 describes arbitrary code execution in Fabric8 Kubernetes Client due to unsafe YAML parsing: a local privileged attacker can supply malicious YAML that is parsed with SnakeYAML default construction. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout 1d1b3d404836871c4d0fc0a35dafe5d40369b519. In that checkout, Serialization.unmarshal wraps the supplied InputStream, peeks at the first non-whitespace byte, and sends non-JSON input into unmarshalYaml. unmarshalYaml constructs SnakeYAML with new Yaml(), calls yaml.load(is), serializes the resulting object map to JSON, and then maps it into the requested Kubernetes resource type. The default SnakeYAML constructor is the vulnerable deserialization/code-generation boundary. Fix commit 445103004d1ed3153d5abb272473451d05891e39 imports SafeConstructor and changes the parser construction to new Yaml(new SafeConstructor()), binding the advisory to source-backed YAML input routing, unsafe SnakeYAML construction, and YAML load of attacker-controlled content.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-44262 / GHSA-65hj-9ppw-77xc describes remote code execution in ff4j versions >= 1.8.1 and < 1.9, patched in 1.9. The exact source snapshot 7c34409d320ed1c917c4ec4ac72a99661c4e446f is the 1.8.13 tag and is inside the affected range. The GHSA-referenced fix commit 62d03140f3bfbd380d0f4b4e5a94dcb8baa9d9c6 merges PR #625 and is contained in tag 1.9. In the vulnerable checkout, FF4J XML, properties, and YAML configuration parsers read attacker-controlled property type and flipstrategy class names from configuration files and instantiate them with Class.forName(...).getConstructor(...).newInstance() or Class.forName(...).newInstance() before checking that the class implements Property or FlippingStrategy. The 1.9 fix adds Property.class.isAssignableFrom and FlippingStrategy.class.isAssignableFrom checks in PropertyFactory, XmlParser, PropertiesParser, and YamlParser. In that checkout, SchemaService.getSchema builds a schema name from the tenant and artifact and only replaces hyphens with underscores, with no allowlist validation. HibernateSchemaService.getSettings stores that schema as HIBERNATE_DEFAULT_SCHEMA, and public createTenant, deleteTenant, and schemaExists flows call schemaExists using tenant-derived schema values. The private schemaExists(Connection, String) builds an information_schema query template containing schema_name = '%s' and executes Statement.executeQuery(String.format(queryTemplate, schema)), directly interpolating the schema value into SQL. Fix commit d374a5f77e6b58e36f0e0e4419be18b95edcd7ff changes schemaExists to a PreparedStatement with a ? parameter and statement.setString(1, schema), and adds a SchemaService regex allowlist [a-zA-Z0-9_]+. This binds the advisory to source-backed tenant-to-schema derivation, unsanitized SQL string formatting, and the database query sink.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-24961 / GHSA-2ccp-vqmv-4r4x describes S3Proxy filesystem and filesystem-nio2 storage backends allowing authenticated clients to traverse outside the intended backing directory. In the reviewed exact prepatch checkout 83b159ee4b9ffcf3f7d91313592fad88feb3b621, AbstractNio2BlobStore uses the request container as a root component and directly resolves attacker-controlled list prefix or object key into filesystem Paths: list() builds pathPrefix as root.resolve(container).resolve(prefix), getBlob() builds root.resolve(container).resolve(key), putBlob() builds root.resolve(container).resolve(blob.getMetadata().getName()) and a similarly derived temp path, removeBlob() deletes containerPath.resolve(key), and getBlobAccess()/setBlobAccess() read or change permissions on root.resolve(container).resolve(key). These paths are used for Files read/write/delete/permission operations without a containment check ensuring the normalized result still starts with the container directory. The S3Proxy 2.6.0 fix commit 86b6ee4749aa163a78e7898efc063617ed171980 is a single-parent commit whose parent is this exact checkout and is titled Prevent parent path traversal in filesystem-nio2; it adds checkValidPath(containerPath, path) and invokes it on list, get, put, delete, get access, and set access paths before filesystem operations. The broader advisory also mentions apache/jclouds@b0819e0 for the non-nio2 backend; this reviewed-source row only admits the source-backed S3Proxy filesystem-nio2 path fixed in this repository commit.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-27505 describes a GeoServer missing-authorization issue where the default REST API security filter protects /rest and subpaths but not extension-style REST index paths such as /rest.html, allowing the REST API index to disclose installed extensions. The exact vulnerable source snapshot dab1947ce0d1a46418ae690734be5ccc5252057b is the GeoServer 2.26.2 release tag, immediately before the fixed 2.26.3 release commit 4a7a6881894a879f097ca2f04d62733fcdaa2937. In the vulnerable default data directory security/config.xml, the rest ServiceLoginFilterChain path is only /rest/** and the gwc ServiceLoginFilterChain path is only /gwc/rest/**. These Ant-style subpath patterns do not cover extension suffix requests such as /rest.html or /gwc/rest.html. The fixed 2.26.3 compare updates data/release/security/config.xml and sample security configs so rest uses /rest.*,/rest/** and gwc uses /gwc/rest.*,/gwc/rest/**, matching the public workaround text. This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable release, and source-backed default security filter path gap without relying on generated findings or non-final sidecar hits.

In the vulnerable default data directory security/config.xml, the rest ServiceLoginFilterChain path is only /rest/** and the gwc ServiceLoginFilterChain path is only /gwc/rest/**. These Ant-style subpath patterns do not cover extension suffix requests such as /rest.html or /gwc/rest.html. The fixed 2.26.3 compare updates data/release/security/config.xml and sample security configs so rest uses /rest.*,/rest/** and gwc uses /gwc/rest.*,/gwc/rest/**, matching the public workaround text. This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable release, and source-backed default security filter path gap without relying on generated findings or non-final sidecar hits.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-30145 / GHSA-gr67-pwcv-76gf describes GeoServer denial of service from malicious Jiffle scripts reachable either as WMS dynamic styling rendering transformations or as WPS processes. The exact vulnerable GeoServer snapshot dab1947ce0d1a46418ae690734be5ccc5252057b is the 2.26.2 release tag, and the fixed GeoServer snapshot 4a7a6881894a879f097ca2f04d62733fcdaa2937 is the 2.26.3 release tag listed as fixed. In the vulnerable checkout, src/pom.xml uses gt.version 32.2 and jaiext.version 1.1.27, while WMS and WPS depend on gt-process-raster, the raster process family that exposes ras:Jiffle in GeoServer rendering transformations and WPS process execution. GeoServer WMS production code extracts SLD FeatureTypeStyle transformations and DirectRasterRenderer applies them through RenderingTransformationHelper; GeoServer test SLDs show ras:Jiffle with a script literal in the same transformation shape. GeoServer WPS production code dispatches ExecuteType to Execute.run and DefaultProcessManager creates and executes the requested GeoTools process with request inputs. The 2.26.3 line updates the GeoTools/JAI-EXT dependency set, including jaiext.version 1.1.31; GeoServer PR #8418 is the 2.26.x backport titled GEOS-11770 Update to jai-ext 1.1.31. In JAI-EXT 1.1.31, the Jiffle compiler/runtime adds MAX_ITERATIONS_KEY, DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS 200, checkLoopIterations(), and inserts checkLoopIterations() into generated while and until loop bodies, with documentation stating that Jiffle limits maximum loop iterations per pixel and throws an exception. This binds the GeoServer entry points and dependency boundary in the vulnerable checkout to the fixed-version Jiffle loop guard without relying on generated findings or non-final sidecar rows.

resolution.evidence: Commit message and diff implement GHSA/CVE described saferedirect normalization and backslash rejection fix.

evidence_refs.evidence: Old source accepts relative redirect paths by checking only raw prefix bytes and then returns the original redirectURL, without normalizing traversal/backslash host separators before http.Redirect can process them.

Patch routes relative paths through normalizeRelativePath, rejects raw and encoded backslashes, path-cleans the redirect, rechecks normalized // or backslash prefixes, and adds path traversal backslash bypass regression tests.

nodes.rationale: The old Probo SafeRedirect.Validate relative-path branch accepts a redirect URL after checking only the raw prefix and the second raw character, then returns the original path. A path such as /../\evil.com can pass the raw check and later be normalized by http.Redirect or browsers into an external-looking redirect. The patch adds normalizeRelativePath, rejects raw and encoded backslashes, cleans the path, and rechecks protocol-relative/backslash prefixes. This is review-entry retrieval ground truth only and does not claim dynamic exploit proof.

vulnerability.description: Geyser is a bridge between Minecraft: Bedrock Edition and Minecraft: Java Edition. Versions of Geyser prior to 1.4.2-SNAPSHOT allow anyone that can connect to the server to forge a LoginPacket with manipulated JWT token allowing impersonation as any user. Version 1.4.2-SNAPSHOT contains a patch for the issue. There are no known workarounds aside from upgrading.

evidence_refs.evidence: Old source returns true for paths beginning with one raw slash unless the second raw byte is slash or backslash, without normalizing encoded backslash or stripped tab/CR/LF separators first.
Patch normalizes raw and encoded backslashes to slash, strips tab/CR/LF, requires a leading slash, rejects normalized //, and adds backslash plus whitespace bypass regression tests.

nodes.rationale: The old Gogs IsSameSite redirect predicate accepts same-site redirect targets with a raw byte check for leading slash, double slash, and a single raw backslash. Browser and framework normalization can turn backslashes, encoded backslashes, or stripped tab/CR/LF separators into network-path redirects after that check. The patch normalizes these separators before requiring a leading slash and rejecting any normalized // sequence. This is review-entry retrieval ground truth only and does not claim dynamic exploit proof.

vulnerability.description: PKCE support is not implemented in accordance with the RFC for OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps. Without the use of PKCE, the authorization code returned by an authorization server is not enough to guarantee that the client that issued the initial authorization request is the one that will be authorized. An attacker is able to obtain the authorization code using a malicious app on the client-side and use it to gain authorization to the protected resource. This affects the package com.google.oauth-client:google-oauth-client before 1.31.0.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-41044 describes partial path traversal in Graylog Support Bundle download/delete APIs: an authenticated admin can access or delete files in sibling directories whose names start with the support-bundle directory prefix. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout d970230b6f3ecb83e07dd43df56428d1421c40e9. In that checkout, SupportBundleResource exposes GET /system/debug/support/bundle/download/{filename} and DELETE /system/debug/support/bundle/{filename}, passing the path parameter filename to SupportBundleService.downloadBundle and deleteBundle. Both service methods call ensureFileWithinBundleDir(filename), then resolve filename under bundleDir and copy or delete the resulting path. The vulnerable ensureFileWithinBundleDir compares bundleDir.resolve(filename).toFile().getCanonicalPath().startsWith(bundleDir.toFile().getCanonicalPath()), which is a string prefix check rather than a path-component containment check, so sibling paths such as support-bundle-test can satisfy the prefix. Fix commit 02b8792e6f4b829f0c1d87fcbf2d58b73458b938 changes the helper to compare normalized absolute Path values and updates both download and delete call sites. This binds the advisory to source-backed filename path parameter intake, weak canonical string-prefix validation, and file read/delete sinks.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-24057 describes Zip Slip style path traversal in HL7 FHIR Core Libraries before 5.6.92, where crafted ZIP or TGZ archives for terminology cache, NPM packages, or comparison archives can carry unsafe entry names. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout 7b22d0355b1b12448e50b9cbfe2a8ae63f2ee828. In that checkout, the R4B and R5 TerminologyCacheManager initialize terminology cache data by downloading tx-cache ZIP content, passing it to unzip, building output paths with Utilities.path(targetDir, ze.getName()), checking the unnormalized string with startsWith(targetDir), and then creating directories or writing entry bytes with TextFile.streamToFileNoClose. Scanner.genScanOutput downloads comparison.zip and Scanner.unzip concatenates destDirectory plus entry.getName directly, then writes files with extractFile or creates directories, without normalizing and verifying destination containment. NpmPackage.readStream also consumes TGZ entry names and loads files without rejecting traversal segments before the fix. Fix commit b50aec59124416b7315a49220cfc3999223414cc adds normalized path checks to terminology cache and scanner ZIP extraction and rejects TGZ entry names containing dot-dot. This binds the advisory to source-backed archive entry name intake, incomplete path traversal validation, and filesystem extraction sinks for ZIP-based cache/comparison archives.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-28465 describes an incomplete fix for CVE-2023-24057 in HL7 FHIR Core Libraries package decompression: normalized archive output paths were still checked with a character string prefix rather than path-component containment, allowing traversal into sibling directories whose names start with the allowed directory name. In that checkout, both R5 and R4B TerminologyCacheManager.initialize download tx-cache ZIP content and call unzip with cacheFolder as targetDir. The unzip methods compute String path = Path.of(Utilities.path(targetDir, ze.getName())).normalize().toFile().getAbsolutePath(), then check if !path.startsWith(targetDir). Because this is String.startsWith, a normalized absolute path under a sibling directory such as cache2 can still start with the targetDir string cache. The methods then create directories or write entry bytes to path. Fix commit 909f7e64fea6532a00b3eb8904bf620fc3cae6d1 changes path to a Path, stores pathString separately for filesystem writes, and checks path.startsWith(Path.of(targetDir).normalize()), using path semantics instead of character-prefix semantics. This binds the advisory to source-backed terminology cache ZIP entry intake, incomplete normalized path containment validation, and filesystem extraction sinks.

In that checkout, both R5 and R4B TerminologyCacheManager.initialize download tx-cache ZIP content and call unzip with cacheFolder as targetDir. The unzip methods compute String path = Path.of(Utilities.path(targetDir, ze.getName())).normalize().toFile().getAbsolutePath(), then check if !path.startsWith(targetDir). Because this is String.startsWith, a normalized absolute path under a sibling directory such as cache2 can still start with the targetDir string cache. The methods then create directories or write entry bytes to path. Fix commit 909f7e64fea6532a00b3eb8904bf620fc3cae6d1 changes path to a Path, stores pathString separately for filesystem writes, and checks path.startsWith(Path.of(targetDir).normalize()), using path semantics instead of character-prefix semantics. This binds the advisory to source-backed terminology cache ZIP entry intake, incomplete normalized path containment validation, and filesystem extraction sinks.

The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout 75b83c55705e38a4e93fbeb3d841779810074924, corresponding to the affected cassandra-4.0.16-1.0.0 source snapshot. In that checkout, the plugin installs a custom IndexQueryHandler as Cassandra CQL query handler. IndexQueryHandler.processStatement prepares bind variables and increments metrics, then intercepts SelectStatement instances carrying Lucene expressions and returns executeLuceneQuery before calling the fallback execute(statement, state, options, requestTime). Unlike Cassandra regular statement execution, this intercepted branch does not call statement.authorize(state.getClientState) or statement.validate(state.getClientState) before evaluating the SELECT and reading data. executeLuceneQuery validates only the Lucene expression, constructs read commands, and either delegates to execute(statement, ...) or performs sorted Lucene reads through executeSortedLuceneQuery and LuceneStorageProxy.read, allowing the Lucene query path to bypass RBAC checks for the selected table. Fix commit 44ab4b639c9354a6335f40b1cf6178c745c6e101, released as cassandra-4.0.17-1.0.0, adds statement.authorize(state.getClientState) and statement.validate(state.getClientState) at the start of processStatement before the Lucene interception. This binds the advisory to source-backed CQL SELECT intake, missing statement authorization and validation, and Lucene read execution sinks.

evidence_refs.evidence: Old source builds the HTTP middleware stack with access logging, memory trim, session, CSRF, and auth middleware, but no TrustedHostMiddleware or configured allowed-host guard.
Patch imports urlparse and TrustedHostMiddleware, derives allowed_host from get_setting('server.http.url'), inserts TrustedHostMiddleware, and adds an attacker Host header 400 regression check.

nodes.rationale: The old IRRd HTTP middleware stack did not install a trusted-host guard before routes that can generate externally visible links from request context. The patch derives an allowed host from configured server.http.url, installs Starlette TrustedHostMiddleware, and adds a wrong Host header integration check returning 400. This is a host-header trust-boundary review entry, not a generic middleware or password-reset-token anchor. This is review-entry retrieval ground truth only and does not claim dynamic exploit proof.

vulnerability.description: pcapture is an open source dumpcap web service interface . In affected versions this vulnerability allows an authenticated but unprivileged user to use the REST API to capture and download packets with no capture filter and without adequate permissions. This is important because the capture filters can effectively limit the scope of information that a user can see in the data captures. If no filter is present, then all data on the local network segment where the program is running can be captured and downloaded. v3.12 fixes this problem. There is no workaround, you must upgrade to v3.12 or greater.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-45206 describes SQL injection in JeecgBoot v3.4.3 through the /sys/duplicate/check component. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout d34614c4224ec1af69d0d81329d84fe98e11f694, which is before the source fix f18ced524c9ec13e876bfb74785a1b112cc8b6bb. In that checkout, DuplicateCheckController exposes GET /sys/duplicate/check and binds request parameters into DuplicateCheckVo fields tableName, fieldName, fieldVal, and dataId. The controller checks only tableName and fieldName with SqlInjectionUtil.filterContent and DictQueryBlackListHandler, then calls SysDictMapper.duplicateCheckCountSql or duplicateCheckCountSqlNoDataId. The mapper XML builds SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ${tableName} WHERE ${fieldName} = #{fieldVal}, using MyBatis ${} substitution for tableName and fieldName, so bypassing the identifier filter reaches raw SQL text. In the vulnerable SqlInjectionUtil, SQL comments matching /\*.*\*/ are stripped before keyword checks, and extractvalue/updatexml are not in the default keyword list. The official fix commit is titled sql注入检查更加严格，修复/sys/duplicate/check存在sql注入漏洞 #4129; it adds SQL_ANNOTATION, calls checkSqlAnnotation before lowercasing, stops stripping comments as a bypass, and adds extractvalue/updatexml to keyword filters. This binds the advisory to source-backed request parameter intake, incomplete SQL injection filtering, and MyBatis dynamic SQL table/field substitution sinks.

CVE-2022-20617 / GHSA-jpxj-vgq5-prjc describes Jenkins Docker Commons Plugin 1.17 and earlier failing to sanitize Docker image names or tags, creating an OS command execution vulnerability for users with Item/Configure permission or control over a configured job SCM repository. The reviewed exact source snapshot 2f0fda49452a7653c33de24220c908786f1aa405 is the vulnerable docker-commons-1.17 source snapshot used by the failed row. In that snapshot, DockerRegistryEndpoint.imageName accepts userAndRepo, checks only for null, and either returns userAndRepo unchanged when url is null or prepends the registry host before returning the same unvalidated image/tag string. This image name is part of the Docker command surface used by downstream Jenkins Docker integrations. The fixed commit c069b79c31c5aa80a01b0c462f0dc6b41751f059 adds ImageNameValidator, calls validateUserAndRepo(userAndRepo) from imageName before returning or prefixing the image string, and validates repository name components and tags with explicit patterns; the added tests reject newline command injection examples such as name:tag\necho hello and name\necho hello:tag plus variable-like image/tag inputs. provenance.rationale: CVE-2019-10392 / SECURITY-1534 affects Jenkins Git Client Plugin 2.8.4 and earlier because repository URL values supplied to CLI git remote operations were not sufficiently restricted before being passed as operands to git ls-remote, allowing crafted values such as command options, --upload-pack, backquoted commands, or whitespace-separated argument sequences to influence command execution on the Jenkins master. The reviewed 2.8.4 source snapshot exposes getHeadRev, getRemoteReferences, and getRemoteSymbolicReferences as remote-reference lookup APIs equivalent to git ls-remote, delegates those APIs through RemoteGitImpl, and in CliGitAPIImpl builds ArgumentListBuilder("ls-remote") before directly appending the caller-controlled url with args.add(url) and invoking launchCommandWithCredentials. The 2.8.5 SECURITY-1534 fix adds GitClientSecurityTest coverage for malicious URL prefixes, introduces addCheckedRemoteUrl to reject dangerous remote URL strings and insert an end-of-options marker, and replaces these direct args.add(url) calls in the ls-remote paths with addCheckedRemoteUrl(args, url). These source spans provide the reviewed command-injection trace and recall anchors for the vulnerable ls-remote URL handling.

vulnerability.description: Jenkins before versions 2.44 and 2.32.2 is vulnerable to an insufficient permission check. This allows users with permissions to create new items (e.g. jobs) to overwrite existing items they don't have access to (SECURITY-321).

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-31720 describes a missing permission check in Jenkins 2.503 and earlier, LTS 2.492.2 and earlier: attackers with Computer/Create permission but without Computer/Extended Read permission can copy an agent and gain access to its configuration. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout dddb4598df25527220a1e0f46d1a0d25217dd4c8. In that checkout, ComputerSet.doCreateItem handles the first POST step for creating a new agent. It checks app.checkPermission(Computer.CREATE), then when mode equals copy, reads the source node name from the from request parameter, resolves Node src = app.getNode(from), serializes the source node with Jenkins.XSTREAM.toXML(src), deserializes it into a new Node, and adds the copied node. There is no src.checkPermission(Computer.EXTENDED_READ) before serializing the source agent configuration. Computer.EXTENDED_READ is a Computer-scoped permission distinct from Computer.CREATE, which is Jenkins-scoped. Fix commit bf32018bf075c06e5df649583557c82d42d8bb5c adds src.checkPermission(Computer.EXTENDED_READ) after resolving the source node and before the XStream copy. This binds the advisory to source-backed HTTP copy-agent intake, missing source-agent extended-read authorization, and source node configuration serialization/copy sinks.

It checks app.checkPermission(Computer.CREATE), then when mode equals copy, reads the source node name from the from request parameter, resolves Node src = app.getNode(from), serializes the source node with Jenkins.XSTREAM.toXML(src), deserializes it into a new Node, and adds the copied node. There is no src.checkPermission(Computer.EXTENDED_READ) before serializing the source agent configuration. Computer.EXTENDED_READ is a Computer-scoped permission distinct from Computer.CREATE, which is Jenkins-scoped. Fix commit bf32018bf075c06e5df649583557c82d42d8bb5c adds src.checkPermission(Computer.EXTENDED_READ) after resolving the source node and before the XStream copy. This binds the advisory to source-backed HTTP copy-agent intake, missing source-agent extended-read authorization, and source node configuration serialization/copy sinks.

nodes.rationale: The source node is serialized with Jenkins.XSTREAM.toXML and deserialized into a new node before being added, exposing source configuration through copy semantics.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-31721 describes an incomplete agent-copy permission fix in Jenkins 2.503 and earlier, LTS 2.492.2 and earlier: attackers with Computer/Create permission but without Computer/Configure permission can copy an agent containing encrypted secrets in its configuration. The failed new-unified row uses exact vulnerable checkout bf32018bf075c06e5df649583557c82d42d8bb5c, which already contains the CVE-2025-31720 Extended Read check but remains vulnerable for secret-bearing agent configurations. In that checkout, ComputerSet.doCreateItem handles POST agent creation, checks Computer.CREATE, enters mode=copy, resolves the source Node from the from request parameter, checks src.checkPermission(Computer.EXTENDED_READ), then serializes the source node with Jenkins.XSTREAM.toXML(src), immediately deserializes it into a new Node, and adds the copied node. The code does not require Computer.CONFIGURE and does not test whether ExtendedReadRedaction would remove secrets from the source configuration before copying. Fix commit b3651b475302e8dba20fc63c1ff89d144ec652f0 adds a guard after XStream serialization: if the user lacks Computer.CONFIGURE, it applies ExtendedReadRedaction.applyAll(xml), compares the redacted XML to the original, and throws AccessDeniedException when the configuration contains redacted secrets. This binds the advisory to source-backed copy-agent HTTP intake, missing configure-or-secret-redaction authorization, and XStream configuration copy sinks.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-24399 affects Jenkins OpenId Connect Authentication Plugin 4.452.v2849b_d3945fa_ and earlier because usernames obtained from a case-sensitive OpenID Connect provider are handed directly to Jenkins authentication and user lookup without a plugin-level case-sensitivity control. In the vulnerable checkout, doFinishLogin reads the configured username claim from the validated OIDC profile and passes it to loginAndSetUserData. loginAndSetUserData then constructs a UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken from that exact string, installs it in the security context, and calls User.get2(token), allowing Jenkins user identity resolution to treat differently cased provider usernames as the same Jenkins user under case-insensitive behavior. Version 4.453.v4d7765c854f4 is documented by GHSA/NVD/Jenkins advisory as introducing an advanced username case-sensitivity option defaulting to case-sensitive.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2020-2261 / GHSA-jq84-6fmm-6qv6 describes OS command execution in Jenkins Perfecto Plugin 1.17 and earlier. Users with Job/Configure permission can configure Perfecto Connect build-wrapper fields so that the plugin executes commands on the Jenkins controller. The reviewed exact source snapshot adabcd9da98628e063bb91198e30ff39a34dc921 corresponds to the vulnerable 1.17 source snapshot used by the failed row. In that snapshot, the DataBoundConstructor stores user-controlled configuration fields including perfectoConnectLocation, perfectoConnectFile, and pcParameters. During setUp, the wrapper reads the Perfecto API key from Jenkins credentials, calls getTunnelId(perfectoConnectLocation, credentials.getCloudName(), apiKey, listener), and getTunnelId builds baseCommand by string-concatenating pcLocation, cloudName, and apiKey, appends pcParameters, then executes the resulting command through cmd.exe /c on Windows or bash -c plus Runtime.getRuntime().exec on Unix. Public advisory text states that Perfecto Plugin 1.18 changes execution to run the specified commands on the agent the build is running on rather than on the controller. The fixed commit 52c09ad2e26416211e4009b095c4f16508b27b8a raw source imports hudson.tasks.CommandInterpreter, builds script = baseCommand + pcParameters, and executes it through getCommandInterpreter(launcher, script), returning Shell(script) on Unix or BatchFile(script) otherwise and calling runner.perform(build, launcher, listener). This binds the advisory, exact vulnerable checkout, source-backed configured-parameter-to-controller-shell-execution path, and fixed-source boundary change.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-24422 / GHSA-76qj-9gwh-pvv3 / Jenkins SECURITY-3016 describe Jenkins Script Security Plugin 1228.vd93135a_2fb_25 and earlier allowing sandboxed Groovy scripts to bypass sandbox protection through map constructor handling, enabling code execution in the Jenkins controller JVM for users allowed to define or run sandboxed scripts. In that snapshot, GroovyCallSiteSelector.constructor treats a single Map argument as Groovy's implicit map constructor and returns a zero-argument constructor when no real constructor matches. provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-31723 / GHSA-hcfh-qjcp-34q9 describes Jenkins Simple Queue Plugin 1.4.6 and earlier not requiring POST requests for multiple HTTP endpoints, allowing CSRF attacks to change and reset the build queue order. The reviewed exact source snapshot c5bc23d6ddd16b0a9792dd05e843a14033e975f1 is the vulnerable source snapshot used by the failed row. In that snapshot, SimpleQueueWidget/index.jelly and SimpleQueueUpdateAction/ajaxBuildQueue.jelly render queue-move controls as plain anchor href links to /simpleMove/move with moveType, itemId, and viewName query parameters. MoveAction.doMove accepts the Stapler request without @RequirePOST, reads those query parameters, locates the Queue.Item, executes move(queue, item, moveType, view), and calls Queue.getInstance().maintain(), so a GET request can mutate build queue ordering when the user has the plugin permission. ResetAction.doReset likewise lacks @RequirePOST and resets the SimpleQueueSorter state. The fixed commit c1094666dcd139830620d6d1c21b13f847601e74 adds @RequirePOST to MoveAction.doMove and ResetAction.doReset and changes both normal and ajax queue widgets from plain <a href=...> controls to <f:link post="true" ...>, binding the public advisory, exact vulnerable checkout, source-backed GET queue mutation path, and the fixed POST/crumb boundary.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-31722 affects Jenkins Templating Engine Plugin 2.5.3 and earlier because libraries defined in folders are not subject to sandbox protection. In exact vulnerable checkout 0af836f6465f80a078a02c6f2ed2e93dd5056213, TemplateFlowDefinition creates a CpsFlowExecution and invokes TemplatePrimitiveInjector.orchestrate. LibraryStepInjector.injectPrimitives loads configured libraries from the governance hierarchy, iterates their steps, and calls StepWrapperFactory.createFromFilePath(stepFile, libName, libConfig) without passing any sandbox/trust decision. StepWrapperFactory.createFromFilePath builds a library StepWrapper and prepareScript always uses exec.getTrustedShell() to parse the library step source. This causes folder-scoped library steps to run through the trusted shell rather than the sandbox shell. Version 2.5.4 changes LibraryStepInjector to distinguish global providers from non-global providers, sets isSandboxed for non-global/folder libraries, passes that flag into createFromFilePath, and changes prepareScript to use exec.getShell() when step.isSandboxed is true.

In that snapshot, SCMSourceRetriever.retrieve resolves the requested library version and calls doRetrieve(name, changelog, scm.build(...), ...). doRetrieve chooses the Jenkins controller workspace and constructs the library checkout directory with baseWorkspace.withSuffix(getFilePathSuffix() + "libs").child(name), so different SCMs sharing a library name share the same controller-side checkout directory. It then allocates that directory and invokes GenericSCMStep.checkout through node.createLauncher(listener), after which files are copied from the checkout into the Pipeline library target. The fixed commit ace0de3c2d691662021ea10306eeb407da6b6365 changes SCMSourceRetriever to compute checkoutDirName = LibraryRecord.directoryNameFor(scm.getKey()) and use child(checkoutDirName), while LibraryRecord adds HMACConfidentialKey-backed directoryNameFor(...). This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable checkout, source-backed shared-library-name-to-controller-checkout path, and fixed SCM-key-derived checkout directory boundary.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-25173 describes Jenkins Pipeline: Groovy Plugin using the same checkout directories for distinct SCMs when reading the Pipeline script file, allowing users with Item/Configure permission to invoke arbitrary OS commands on the controller through crafted SCM contents. The reviewed exact source snapshot 6ed3b5b01ff16dc4f6f9f4b209dbc21394b13913 is the vulnerable source snapshot used by the failed row. In that snapshot, CpsScmFlowDefinition.create expands the configured scriptPath, falls back to a heavyweight controller checkout, computes dir = getFilePathWithSuffix(baseWorkspace), and getFilePathWithSuffix returns baseWorkspace.withSuffix(getFilePathSuffix() + "script") without any SCM-specific component. The code then checks out the configured SCM into that shared directory using GenericSCMStep.checkout with node.createLauncher(listener), obtains scriptFile = dir.child(expandedScriptPath), and performs only an absolutize/string-prefix containment check before reading the script. The fixed commit f7ae7b75a457976853539bff1db52373b85fdb85 adds HMACConfidentialKey CHECKOUT_DIR_KEY, changes getFilePathWithSuffix(baseWorkspace, scm) to append CHECKOUT_DIR_KEY.mac(scm.getKey()), writes the SCM key for debugging, and replaces the raw absolutize string-prefix check with a canonical File path startsWith check. This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable checkout, shared checkout directory and weak containment path, and fixed SCM-key-derived directory plus canonical containment boundary.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-25175 describes Jenkins Pipeline: Multibranch Plugin using the same checkout directories for distinct SCMs for the readTrusted step, allowing users with Item/Configure permission to invoke arbitrary OS commands on the controller through crafted SCM contents. The reviewed exact source snapshot d43c65dec013812b084fecbb4a310d856eb6b89a is the vulnerable source snapshot used by the failed row. In that snapshot, ReadTrustedStep.Execution.run obtains the Jenkins controller base workspace, computes dir = getFilePathWithSuffix(baseWorkspace), derives file = dir.child(step.path), and performs only an absolutize/string-prefix containment check before checkout. Both standalone SCM and multibranch trusted/tip flows then perform GenericSCMStep.checkout into the same non-SCM-specific directory with node.createLauncher(listener) and read file content from that directory. The fixed commit 71c3f0a6ccdb2ba43f43686826b0d62160df85e8 adds an HMACConfidentialKey shared with CpsScmFlowDefinition, changes getFilePathWithSuffix(baseWorkspace, scm) to append CHECKOUT_DIR_KEY.mac(scm.getKey()), writes the SCM key for debugging, and adds isDescendant based on File.getCanonicalFile before reading files. This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable checkout, source-backed readTrusted shared checkout path, and fixed SCM-key-derived directory plus canonical containment guard.

nodes.rationale: The helper returns baseWorkspace.withSuffix(getFilePathSuffix() + "script") without incorporating the SCM key. The fix adds getFilePathWithSuffix(baseWorkspace, scm) and CHECKOUT_DIR_KEY.mac(scm.getKey()).

provenance.rationale: CVE-2018-12036 affects OWASP Dependency-Check before 3.2.0 because crafted archive entry names can escape the intended extraction directory. In exact vulnerable checkout c3b5b3c0d7fe7283b4cd421149d6fb620476f67d, ArchiveAnalyzer.extractFiles opens zip/tar archives and dispatches them into extractArchive. ArchiveAnalyzer.extractArchive constructs new File(destination, entry.getName()) for every archive entry and extractAcceptedFile writes that file with FileOutputStream without canonicalizing the resulting path or checking that it remains under destination. The same pattern appears in ExtractionUtil.extractFiles for ZipInputStream and ExtractionUtil.extractArchive/extractFile for ArchiveInputStream: directory and file outputs are built from extractTo/destination plus entry.getName() and then created or written directly. A malicious entry such as ../outside can therefore target a path outside the temporary extraction directory. Version 3.2.0 adds destination.getCanonicalPath() checks in ArchiveAnalyzer for compressed outputs and archive entries, and in ExtractionUtil for ZipInputStream and ArchiveInputStream extraction, rejecting entries whose canonical output path does not start with the destination path.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-1948 describes Eclipse Jetty 12.0.0 through 12.0.16 accepting an excessively large HTTP/2 SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE from a client and using it for HPACK response encoding, which can drive large ByteBuffer allocation and denial of service. The residual source snapshot 8414f79a9c476ecb78998c8ce88f0c5ae548f7e6 is itself the fix commit '#12690 cap MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE', so the reviewed-source evidence must bind the case to its parent prepatch checkout 487f7e710219b50f4b8e960444477fd1638ee4ce. In that prepatch checkout, HTTP2Session handles SettingsFrame.MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE and directly calls generator.getHpackEncoder().setMaxHeaderListSize(value) for remote/client settings. HpackEncoder.setMaxHeaderListSize assigns the provided value directly to _maxHeaderListSize. The fix commit changes the remote setting path to cap the encoder value with Math.min(value, hpackEncoder.getMaxHeaderListSize()) and changes setMaxHeaderListSize to fall back to the default for non-positive values; it also adds SettingsTest.testMaxHeaderListSizeCappedByClient to exercise the client-advertised oversized setting. These spans bind the vulnerable prepatch behavior to the exact parent of the public fix commit.

The exact vulnerable source snapshot 9ce20009d6bf726086fc528fceb174933077bff4 exposes Html.provider() and Html.of() as the default text/html escaper, but its documented escaped characters are only double quote, greater-than, less-than, and ampersand. provenance.rationale: CVE-2014-3656 describes cross-site scripting in JBoss Keycloak login-status-iframe.html. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 3b071b83aa0444749eba851fdbe0f2ed47932410, where integration/js/src/main/resources/login-status-iframe.html registers a message event handler. In that vulnerable snapshot, receiveMessage checks event.origin against the built origin, then directly mutates event.data by assigning loggedIn and session fields, reads the KEYCLOAK_SESSION cookie, and sends the same event.data object back with postMessage. This means message payload handling relies on a caller-supplied object crossing the postMessage boundary rather than a serialized data contract, matching the iframe XSS location named by NVD. Fix commit ce1fd8eedcaa814a647f42fdf45de718fa5bfc7f is titled using JSON.stringify(...) and JSON.parse(...); its patch changes the same file so receiveMessage parses event.data with JSON.parse, writes loggedIn/session to the parsed data object, and sends JSON.stringify(data) instead of event.data. This binds the advisory to source-backed postMessage intake, unsafe event.data mutation/echo, session-cookie propagation, and the JSON serialization fix in the named iframe resource.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-1274 / GHSA-m4fv-gm5m-4725 describes HTML injection in the Keycloak Admin REST API execute-actions-email endpoint: arbitrary HTML can be injected into emails sent to users, enabling phishing. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 4d0629dcf424d805857bec33214e8eb3c0cb781b. In that checkout, UserResource.executeActionsEmail exposes PUT @Path("execute-actions-email") and consumes a JSON List<String> actions. The method checks user, client, redirect URI, and lifespan, but does not validate that actions contains only registered required action identifiers. It constructs an ExecuteActionsActionToken with the caller-provided actions, then passes token.getRequiredActions() into EmailTemplateProvider as Constants.TEMPLATE_ATTR_REQUIRED_ACTIONS and calls sendExecuteActions. FreeMarkerEmailTemplateProvider stores arbitrary template attributes, builds the executeActions.ftl template, and sends the resulting HTML body through EmailSenderProvider. The HTML executeActions.ftl template builds requiredActionsText by iterating requiredActions and interpolating each reqActionItem into msg("requiredAction.${reqActionItem}"), then embeds requiredActionsText into executeActionsBodyHtml with kcSanitize(...)?no_esc. Fix commit fc3c61235fa30132123c17ed8702ff7b3a672fe9 adds RequiredActionsValidator.validRequiredActions(session, actions) to UserResource.executeActionsEmail before token and template construction, rejecting invalid required action values. This binds the advisory to source-backed Admin REST actions intake, missing required-action validation, email-template interpolation, and HTML email sending sinks.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-3782 / GHSA-g8q8-fggx-9r3q describes a Keycloak path traversal / redirect validation bypass via double URL encoding for clients using wildcard Valid Redirect URIs. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout cce8ee2b1ab7c925bfbb62d8f12a33e93d943040. In that checkout, AuthorizationEndpoint accepts GET/POST authorization parameters, AuthorizationEndpointChecker.checkRedirectUri reads request.getRedirectUriParam() and calls RedirectUtils.verifyRedirectUri. LogoutEndpoint similarly accepts post_logout_redirect_uri or legacy redirect_uri and calls RedirectUtils.verifyRedirectUri for client post-logout redirects. The shared RedirectUtils.verifyRedirectUri implementation creates a URI directly from the supplied redirectUri and normalizes it, then lower-cases the hostname and checks the still-encoded string against resolved valid redirects. Its wildcard matcher accepts a redirect when the request string starts with the configured wildcard prefix. There is no repeated decoding of the path component before normalization and wildcard matching, so double-encoded traversal segments can survive validation. Fix commit 1987c942f527b9f3bbf2a86ba71ba8ae0154ac37 adds decodeRedirectUri to RedirectUtils, invokes it before URI.create/normalize, decodes the redirect URL up to five times while preserving query and fragment, and adds regression tests for encoded and double-encoded ../ patterns. This binds the advisory to source-backed OIDC redirect parameter intake, missing multi-decode before redirect validation, wildcard prefix matching, and the production-source decode fix.

The base login code.ftl template renders msg("codeErrorTitle", code.error) and code.error directly, without kcSanitize(...). The pre-fix KeycloakSanitizerMethod sanitizes the immediate string only and lacks the decodeHtmlFull() loop added by the fix. The fix commit removes the message attribute for CODE pages, wraps both code error render sites in kcSanitize(...), imports org.owasp.html.Encoding, and adds decodeHtmlFull() before sanitizer policy application, binding the advisory to source-backed OOB endpoint, template rendering, and sanitizer changes.

evidence_refs.evidence: Old preserved source shows matchesRedirects at corrected lines 232-249 returning a boolean after wildcard prefix/equality matching.
Patch returns matched redirect pattern and rejects unsafe schemes unless explicitly allowed.

nodes.rationale: Manual span repair confirms that the preserved old source places RedirectUtils.matchesRedirects at lines 232-249, not the candidate-pool extracted 206-228 span retained in Phase 21.092. The helper performs wildcard prefix/equality matching and returns only a boolean, so the caller cannot know which configured redirect pattern matched for non-http scheme validation. The patch changes the helper to return the matched pattern and rejects unsafe schemes unless explicitly allowed. This checkpoint repairs one existing label only; it does not add labels, run retrieval, or claim dynamic exploit proof.

nodes.rationale: Manual repair confirms an open-redirect validation source contract: caller-controlled redirectUri is decoded, normalized, matched against wildcard-capable valid redirect patterns, and accepted without retaining the matched pattern for scheme validation. This checkpoint repairs metadata only; it does not add labels, run retrieval, or claim dynamic exploit proof.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-0604 / GHSA-2p82-5wwr-43cw describes Keycloak LDAP federation authentication bypass after reset credentials: an Active Directory user can reset a password and remain logged in without a fresh LDAP bind that would enforce disabled or expired AD account state. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout b70303f2932dabd5f462128b1dc8a3d2640799a2. In that checkout, ResetCredentialEmail.authenticate handles the reset-credential-email authenticator. When the user returns via the reset credentials action token, it detects DefaultActionTokenKey.ACTION_TOKEN_USER_ID, logs that it is skipping the reset email screen, immediately calls context.success(), and returns. The authenticator is not configurable, configuredFor always returns true, and there is no force-login behavior for federated users. ResetPassword then adds the UPDATE_PASSWORD required action and succeeds, and UpdatePassword updates the user password through user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...) followed by context.success(). This source path allows the reset-credentials flow to continue in the same authentication session after password update instead of forcing a fresh login path for LDAP/federated users. The production-source fix chain first adds a force-login option in commit 66a6248d519718d5b8c8800d52ffa46074ee9437, then commit 707a5568284c615393cc8d47857a2aae05dd2864 changes ResetCredentialEmail to use forceLogin(context.getAuthenticatorConfig(), user), changes the option default to only-federated, and implements forceLogin so federated users identified by non-local StorageId or federationLink get AuthenticationManager.END_AFTER_REQUIRED_ACTIONS set after reset credentials. This binds the advisory to source-backed reset credential action-token reauth, password update required action, missing federated-user forced re-login, and the LDAP/federated force-login production fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-3501 / GHSA-HW58-3793-42GG describes a Keycloak hostname-verification flaw where setting the TLS hostname verifier policy to ANY causes truststore certificate verification for outgoing HTTPS/SMTP trust managers to be skipped. In that checkout, TruststoreOptions exposes the tls-hostname-verifier option with HostnameVerificationPolicy values, and JSSETruststoreConfigurator.getTrustManagers() checks getProvider().getPolicy() == HostnameVerificationPolicy.ANY before returning a custom X509TrustManager. This binds the advisory to source-backed tls-hostname-verifier configuration, truststore provider policy selection, no-op X509TrustManager creation, and the production-source removal of the ANY trust-manager bypass.

In that checkout, TruststoreOptions exposes the tls-hostname-verifier option with HostnameVerificationPolicy values, and JSSETruststoreConfigurator.getTrustManagers() checks getProvider().getPolicy() == HostnameVerificationPolicy.ANY before returning a custom X509TrustManager. That trust manager returns an empty accepted issuer array and leaves both checkClientTrusted and checkServerTrusted empty, bypassing the TrustManagerFactory path that would initialize from provider.getTruststore(). Fix commit 99ca24c832729075e04d8bc58666089268314272 removes this HostnameVerificationPolicy.ANY special branch from JSSETruststoreConfigurator and updates truststore option documentation to state that ANY should not be used in production. This binds the advisory to source-backed tls-hostname-verifier configuration, truststore provider policy selection, no-op X509TrustManager creation, and the production-source removal of the ANY trust-manager bypass.

nodes.rationale: The normal path initializes TrustManagerFactory with provider.getTruststore() and returns those trust managers; the ANY branch bypasses this validation path.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-3910 allows circumventing administrator-required actions such as 2FA setup through login URL action manipulation. The vulnerable checkout passes kcAction != null into executeAction, treating any requested kc_action as action-initiated execution even when the first applicable required action is a different user/admin-required action. In the IGNORE path it removes the required action and records SUCCESS, allowing a required action to be skipped. PR #39351 fixes this by passing kcActionExecution only when kcAction equals the selected provider id and by no longer removing required actions on IGNORE.

nodes.rationale: executionActions chooses the first applicable required action but passes kcAction != null to executeAction. If a login URL contains a kc_action parameter while an administrator-required action such as OTP setup is pending, this boolean can classify the selected action as app-initiated action execution rather than a regular required action.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-7365 / GHSA-xhpr-465j-7p9q describes a Keycloak phishing/account-linking flaw in the first broker login flow: after an authenticated attacker reaches the IdP account merge/review-profile path, the attacker can change the reviewed email address to a victim address and still use the Verify Existing Account By Email execution, causing a verification email that can link the external identity to the victim account. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 1183157d862f9ccc66e1d6b36018e1aea6d49046. In that checkout, AbstractIdentityProvider defines only UPDATE_PROFILE_EMAIL_CHANGED for the review page, IdpReviewProfileAuthenticator.processAction records the email-changed note when the review profile email attribute changes, and IdpConfirmLinkAuthenticator lets the user choose updateProfile before linkAccount. IdpEmailVerificationAuthenticator.authenticateImpl then proceeds from SMTP availability directly to existing-user lookup and sendVerifyEmail unless the VERIFY_ACCOUNT_IDP_USERNAME auth note already matches the broker username; it does not check the review-profile changed email note, and there is no username-changed note at all. sendVerifyEmail builds an IdpVerifyAccountLinkActionToken for the existing user email and sends the confirm identity broker link message. Fix commit b5d6c8c4021717e26eccfe041dba4fbc81e5f186 records username changes, checks UPDATE_PROFILE_USERNAME_CHANGED or UPDATE_PROFILE_EMAIL_CHANGED before email verification, calls context.attempted() when either changed, and hides the review button unless the review execution previously succeeded. This binds the advisory to source-backed first-broker-login review-profile mutation, missing changed-profile gate before email verification, verification-token email dispatch, and the production-source fix that disables email verification after manual review changes.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-7784 / GHSA-27gp-8389-hm4w describes a Keycloak FGAPv2 privilege escalation where an administrator with manage-users style authority could escalate to realm-admin because fine-grained admin permission checks around admin role mappings did not require a server administrator. The exact vulnerable source snapshot 73e5f4bead7840f19210aaabcbd1a00895d46929 is the Keycloak 26.2.5 release tag in the affected range before 26.2.6. The fixed source snapshot 51bd67030d264a6f001de425ce558fad55970336 is the Keycloak 26.2.6 release tag, whose release notes state that admin role mappings are restricted to server administrators. In the vulnerable checkout, UserResource exposes /role-mappings for a user with manageCheck bound to auth.users().requireMapRoles(user). RoleMapperResource.addRealmRoleMappings first requires that manage permission, then for each requested realm role calls auth.roles().requireMapRole(roleModel) before granting the role. RolePermissionsV2.canMapRole returns checkAdminRoles(role) for admins with MANAGE_USERS and also combines hasPermission(...MAP_ROLE_SCOPE) with checkAdminRoles(role). The inherited checkAdminRoles accepts admin roles in the realm-management client by checking similar realm-level permissions such as root.users().canManage() for MANAGE_USERS, rather than requiring a master-realm server admin. The 26.2.6 fix adds hasMasterAdminRole() and denies AdminRoles.ALL_ROLES mapping in canMapRole/canMapComposite unless the acting admin has the master realm admin role; it also removes the old checkAdminRoles gating from the FGAPv2 canMapRole return path. This binds the advisory to source-backed role mapping entrypoints and the fixed permission boundary.

The exact vulnerable source snapshot 73e5f4bead7840f19210aaabcbd1a00895d46929 is the Keycloak 26.2.5 release tag in the affected range before 26.2.6. The fixed source snapshot 51bd67030d264a6f001de425ce558fad55970336 is the Keycloak 26.2.6 release tag, whose release notes state that admin role mappings are restricted to server administrators. In the vulnerable checkout, UserResource exposes /role-mappings for a user with manageCheck bound to auth.users().requireMapRoles(user). RoleMapperResource.addRealmRoleMappings first requires that manage permission, then for each requested realm role calls auth.roles().requireMapRole(roleModel) before granting the role. RolePermissionsV2.canMapRole returns checkAdminRoles(role) for admins with MANAGE_USERS and also combines hasPermission(...MAP_ROLE_SCOPE) with checkAdminRoles(role). The inherited checkAdminRoles accepts admin roles in the realm-management client by checking similar realm-level permissions such as root.users().canManage() for MANAGE_USERS, rather than requiring a master-realm server admin. The 26.2.6 fix adds hasMasterAdminRole() and denies AdminRoles.ALL_ROLES mapping in canMapRole/canMapComposite unless the acting admin has the master realm admin role; it also removes the old checkAdminRoles gating from the FGAPv2 canMapRole return path. This binds the advisory to source-backed role mapping entrypoints and the fixed permission boundary.

nodes.rationale: In FGAPv2, canMapRoles returns true for admins with MANAGE_USERS before falling back to fine-grained MAP_ROLES permission, providing the source-backed user role mapping permission path.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2020-8570 / GHSA-cghx-9gcr-r42x describes a path traversal flaw in the Java Kubernetes Client copy-from-pod implementation: copying multiple files from a malicious pod can extract entries outside the requested destination directory when the pod returns a crafted tar archive. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 796c74f4244cacd90d99393640ccaad0c72f8893. In that checkout, Copy.copyDirectoryFromPod verifies tar availability, executes `tar cz - <srcPath> | base64` inside the target pod, decodes the process output through Base64InputStream, GzipCompressorInputStream, and TarArchiveInputStream, iterates each ArchiveEntry, and constructs the local destination with new File(destination.toFile(), entry.getName()). It then creates directories and writes file bytes without normalizing the archive entry name or ensuring the resulting path remains under the destination directory. Fix commit eb2cfe945c1492503b086606734530550630d31f adds commons-io FilenameUtils and changes this construction to FilenameUtils.normalize(entry.getName()), rejecting null normalized names before building the destination File. This binds the advisory to source-backed pod tar archive intake, archive-entry name trust, destination path construction, and the production-source normalization fix.

It then creates directories and writes file bytes without normalizing the archive entry name or ensuring the resulting path remains under the destination directory. Fix commit eb2cfe945c1492503b086606734530550630d31f adds commons-io FilenameUtils and changes this construction to FilenameUtils.normalize(entry.getName()), rejecting null normalized names before building the destination File. This binds the advisory to source-backed pod tar archive intake, archive-entry name trust, destination path construction, and the production-source normalization fix.

nodes.rationale: The constructed File is used to create parent directories and write archive bytes, so a traversal entry name can direct writes outside the intended destination.

In this checkout, MapPrinterServlet exposes multiple GET JSON endpoints that accept a jsonp request parameter, switch the response content type to application/javascript when the parameter is non-empty, and write the callback string directly before and after JSON output. The GHSA-linked fix commit 89155f2506b9cee822e15ce60ccae390a1419d5e is titled Remove JSONP support and deletes the jsonp request parameters, callback wrapping, and JavaScript content type path from MapPrinterServlet; it is contained in 3.24.0. The reviewed spans below bind the exact 3.22 source snapshot to the public JSONP XSS path without relying on eval hits, generated source-sink annotations, or non-final sidecar proxies.

vulnerability.description: Micronaut Security is a security solution for applications. Prior to versions 3.1.2, 3.2.4, 3.3.2, 3.4.3, 3.5.3, 3.6.6, 3.7.4, 3.8.4, 3.9.6, 3.10.2, and 3.11.1, IdTokenClaimsValidator skips `aud` claim validation if token is issued by same identity issuer/provider. Any OIDC setup using Micronaut where multiple OIDC applications exists for the same issuer but token auth are not meant to be shared. This issue has been patched in versions 3.1.2, 3.2.4, 3.3.2, 3.4.3, 3.5.3, 3.6.6, 3.7.4, 3.8.4, 3.9.6, 3.10.2, and 3.11.1.

vulnerability_trace.summary:
在校验 issuer, audience 和 azp 时，存在逻辑缺陷，导致当同一 issuer 下存在多个客户端时，跳过了对 clientId 和 azp 的校验，存在未授权访问风险。
```java
issuer.equalsIgnoreCase(iss) || <--- 错误的逻辑操作符，应为 &&
  audiences.contains(clientId) &&
  validateAzp(claims, clientId, audiences);
```

当用户设置 `micronaut.security.authentication` 为 `idtoken` 时，校验不符合 openID 文档给出的流程要求，没有验证 aud
https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDTokenValidation

> Clients MUST validate the ID Token in the Token Response in the following manner:
...
> 1.2. The Issuer Identifier for the OpenID Provider (which is typically obtained during Discovery) MUST exactly match the value of the iss (issuer) Claim.
> 1.3. The Client MUST validate that the aud (audience) Claim contains its client_id value registered at the Issuer identified by the iss (issuer) Claim as an audience.

patch 代码：
```diff
@@ -199,7 +199,7 @@ protected boolean validateIssuerAudienceAndAzp(@NonNull JwtClaims claims,
            Optional<URL> issuerOptional = openIdClientConfiguration.getIssuer();
            if (issuerOptional.isPresent()) {
                String issuer = issuerOptional.get().toString();
-                return issuer.equalsIgnoreCase(iss) ||
+                return issuer.equalsIgnoreCase(iss) &&
                        audiences.contains(clientId) &&
                                validateAzp(claims, clientId, audiences);
            }
```

browser backslash normalization can turn a relative-looking redirect target into a protocol-relative external host

nodes.rationale: IsRelativePath accepts a redirect target as local when Go url.Parse sees no scheme or host. The old code does not reject backslashes before parser validation, while browsers normalize backslashes to slashes. The patch adds an explicit strings.Contains(link, "\\") rejection before url.Parse, confirming this function as the open-redirect review entry.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2016-10006 / GHSA-683w-6h9j-57wq describes an AntiSamy XSS bypass before 1.5.5 where a specially crafted tag that supports style with active content can bypass library protections. The upstream issue is titled Style validation in attributes is not properly handled, and fix commit 7313931dc3c0d1377b010f07faef2063dd359a36 is titled Updated for proper style tag validation, stating that it validated style tag attributes to fix style tag XSS in MagicSAXFilter.java. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 8bebe1eb2ec1ac23e34111e9d06024d7dab7fa25, immediately before that fix. In that checkout, MagicSAXFilter.startElement detects a validate-action style tag and immediately pushes Ops.CSS, initializes cssContent, and stores cssAttributes = attributes. This branch bypasses the generic attribute validation loop that scans inline style attributes, checks allowed attributes and expressions, and builds validattributes. Later, characters() records only style element text while in Ops.CSS, and endElement() scans cssContent with CssScanner but emits the style element using super.startElement(element, cssAttributes, ...), preserving the original unvalidated style tag attributes. The fix moves style tag CSS mode after the generic attribute validation and assigns cssAttributes = validattributes, binding the advisory to source-backed style-tag attribute bypass, CSS content scanning, unvalidated attribute writeback, and the production-source validation fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2017-14735 describes OWASP AntiSamy before 1.5.7 allowing XSS through HTML5 entities, demonstrated by using : to construct a javascript: URL. The v1.5.7 tag commit e76f02a77afb4e43b897f13d17b5bc1260b8afde is titled Release version 1.5.7 and its message references Issue #10 with policy updates sensitive to the html5 colon entity. Its parent c48ed190a8e8e374444588ef43bb058dced3b93f is the reviewed prepatch checkout. In that prepatch checkout, antisamy.xml defines onsiteURL as a permissive character-class expression that includes ampersand and semicolon, and href accepts onsiteURL before offsiteURL. The existing tests reject literal javascript: and numeric-entity javascript payloads, but the later fix adds a new issue10 regression asserting that javascript:alert(1) is removed in both DOM and SAX modes. The fix changes all bundled onsiteURL regexes to a negative lookahead that rejects &colon and adds anchoredURL separately, binding the vulnerable prepatch policy behavior to the patched 1.5.7 release.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-28367 / GHSA-3pqg-4rqg-pg9g describes an AntiSamy XSS issue where STYLE tag content could be smuggled because the DOM scanner did not properly encode or sanitize CSS content split across multiple child nodes. In the exact vulnerable source snapshot b7c151112dd19928e700ee48639942fd1079d1e3, AntiSamyDOMScanner.actionValidate special-cases style tags and delegates them to processStyleTag(), but processStyleTag() reads only ele.getFirstChild(), scans firstChild.getNodeValue() with CssScanner, and writes the cleaned CSS back only to that first child. Additional child nodes under the style element are neither included in toScan nor removed after cleaning, so attacker-controlled markup split into later STYLE children can survive the CSS scanner path. The fixing commit 0199e7e194dba5e7d7197703f43ebe22401e61ae is titled "Support multiple children handling on style tags" and changes processStyleTag() to concatenate textContent from every child node, scan the combined CSS text, set the cleaned result on the first child, and remove all remaining child nodes; the added test covers a smuggled input containing <style><script>alert(1)</script></style>@import.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-29577 / GHSA-vp37-2f9p-3vr3 describes an AntiSamy XSS issue that exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2022-28367. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout b6e76de85a07549f2c97941437dd73430d7287a8. In that checkout, AntiSamyDOMScanner.actionValidate routes style tags to processStyleTag before normal child processing. processStyleTag concatenates textContent from every child node and scans the combined CSS with CssScanner, then writes the clean CSS into the first child. However, it removes remaining child nodes with a forward loop over ele.getChildNodes().getLength() starting at index 1 while the NodeList is updated by each removal. That live-list forward deletion can skip later child nodes, leaving attacker-controlled smuggled nodes under the style element after CSS cleaning. Fix commit 32e273507da0e964b58c50fd8a4c94c9d9363af0 stores the original childNodesCount and removes extra children from childNodesCount - 1 down to 1, explicitly noting the reverse order is needed because the list updates on the fly. The added regression tests cover smuggled input containing select/style/input and assert that DOM and SAX output do not contain the injected input. This binds the advisory to source-backed style-tag dispatch, multi-child CSS text aggregation, first-child clean writeback, live NodeList forward-removal skip, and the production-source reverse-removal fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-27508 / GHSA-hw43-fcmm-3m5g describes Emissary exposing ChecksumCalculator for hashing and checksum generation with weak or non-cryptographic algorithms such as SHA-1 and CRC32, creating risk if the utility is used for security-sensitive guarantees. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout ff9fed1d5910ca1879a290b78045ec991a93cb2e. In that checkout, src/main/java/emissary/kff/ChecksumCalculator.java declares a public ChecksumCalculator class documented only as a utility for checksums and message digests. Its public no-argument constructor initializes SHA-1 and enables CRC32 by default, and other public constructors accept arbitrary algorithm names or collections, with explicit support for CRC32 and SSDEEP. The digest(byte[]) and digest(SeekableByteChannelFactory) methods compute configured MessageDigest values, CRC32, and ssdeep and place them into ChecksumResults. Fix commit da3a81a8977577597ff2a944820a5ae4e9762368 makes the class and its constructors package-private, documents that it is for KFF/document similarity only, and states it is not meant to provide cryptographically secure hashes or checksums. This binds the advisory to source-backed public API exposure, weak/default algorithm selection, digest/checksum output, and the production-source visibility and documentation fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-24970 / GHSA-4g8c-wm8x-jfhw describes a Netty SslHandler validation issue where a specially crafted packet can trigger a native crash when the native SSLEngine is used. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout d1fbda62d3a47835d3fb35db8bd42ecc205a5386, which is the direct parent of fix commit 87f40725155b2f89adfde68c7732f97c153676c4. In that checkout, SslHandler.decode routes inbound encrypted bytes to decodeJdkCompatible, reads packetLength with SslUtils.getEncryptedPacketLength, handles NOT_ENCRYPTED and NOT_ENOUGH_DATA, and then calls unwrap with that packetLength. The vulnerable SslUtils.getEncryptedPacketLength(ByteBuf, offset, probeSSLv2) immediately reads content type, protocol version, and length fields from the supplied offset without first checking that the remaining data covers the TLS record header, and its DTLS check uses buffer.readableBytes() against offset + DTLS_RECORD_HEADER_LENGTH rather than remaining bytes from the offset. The ByteBuffer[] path copies into a five-byte temporary buffer until full without bounding the loop by the available buffers, and the ByteBuffer parser also reads header fields before checking remaining length. ReferenceCountedOpenSslEngine.unwrap calls SslUtils.getEncryptedPacketLength(srcs, srcsOffset), handles NOT_ENCRYPTED only, and then subtracts SSL_RECORD_HEADER_LENGTH from packetLength; before the fix there is no assertion that packetLength is non-negative. Fix commit 87f40725155b2f89adfde68c7732f97c153676c4 adds remaining-length checks that return NOT_ENOUGH_DATA, bounds the ByteBuffer[] copy loop, changes empty SSLv2-style records to NOT_ENCRYPTED, and asserts packetLength >= 0 before native unwrap sizing. This binds the advisory to source-backed SslHandler packet validation, incomplete TLS/DTLS header length checks, native OpenSSL unwrap packet sizing, and the production-source validation fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-25193 / GHSA-389x-839f-4rhx describes a Netty denial of service on Windows where the previous large-file mitigation was incomplete because null bytes were not counted against the input limit. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout f844d78e4e23182610a24576d225de933f90f92e, which is the direct parent of fix commit d1fbda62d3a47835d3fb35db8bd42ecc205a5386. In that checkout, BoundedInputStream stores maxBytesRead and numRead, but its single-byte read() increments numRead only when the returned byte value is greater than zero. Java InputStream.read returns byte values from 0 to 255 and -1 for EOF, so a valid 0x00 byte is read but not counted. The bulk read(byte[], off, len) path similarly increments numRead only when the return count is greater than zero, and both paths call checkMaxBytesRead after the read, allowing the zero-byte stream case named by the advisory to bypass the bound. The existing vulnerable test only uses random bytes and has no deterministic all-byte/null-byte coverage. Fix commit d1fbda62d3a47835d3fb35db8bd42ecc205a5386 changes both read paths to count every value except -1, removes the post-read check so reads are truncated to the limit before failing on the next read, and adds deterministic testBoundEnforced256 coverage for all byte values including 0x00. This binds the advisory to source-backed BoundedInputStream byte-counting behavior, the null-byte bound bypass, and the production-source fix that counts valid zero bytes.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-29908 / GHSA-HQQC-JR88-P6X2 describes a Netty QUIC hash-collision denial of service where remote attackers can send packets with colliding Source Connection IDs and drive excessive CPU through the connection-id map. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout dca355aa8a1f63dfaf6aa2fe88734e4bd5314c14. In that checkout, QuicheQuicCodec stores connection IDs in a plain HashMap keyed by ByteBuffer. Incoming DatagramPacket content is parsed by QuicHeaderParser, which passes parsed SCID and DCID into quicPacketRead. The codec then tracks active channel source connection IDs with direct HashMap get, put, remove, clear, and add/remove mapping operations. New and retired source connection IDs returned by a channel are inserted into or removed from the same HashMap. Fix commit e059bd9b78723f8b035e0c547e42ce263f03461c replaces the plain HashMap with ConnectionIdChannelMap backed by SipHash 1-3 using random keys, explicitly to prevent connection-id hash collision attacks. This binds the advisory to source-backed datagram-to-header processing, SCID/DCID channel dispatch, vulnerable ByteBuffer HashMap storage, source-connection-id mapping updates, and the production-source SipHash map fix.

vulnerability.description: Common is a package of common modules that can be accessed by NIMBLE services. Common before commit number 3b96cb0293d3443b870351945f41d7d55cb34b53 did not properly verify the signature of JSON Web Tokens. This allows someone to forge a valid JWT. Being able to forge JWTs may lead to authentication bypasses. Commit number 3b96cb0293d3443b870351945f41d7d55cb34b53 contains a patch for the issue. As a workaround, one may use the parseClaimsJws method to correctly verify the signature of a JWT.

evidence_refs.evidence: Old source emits SSR redirect Location/meta-refresh values while encodeURL returns same-origin url.pathname without collapsing multiple leading slashes.
Patch collapses leading slashes in encodeURL, derives meta refresh from the encoded header, and adds protocol-relative path-normalization regression tests.

nodes.rationale: The Nuxt SSR navigateTo path writes both an HTML meta refresh URL and a Location header from the same redirect location. Old source HTML-escaped the raw location before encodeURL collapsed or normalized same-origin path output, while the patch derives the HTML attribute from the encoded header value. This is review-entry retrieval ground truth only and does not claim dynamic exploit proof.

vulnerability.description: In Opencast before 7.6 and 8.1, using a remember-me cookie with an arbitrary username can cause Opencast to assume proper authentication for that user even if the remember-me cookie was incorrect given that the attacked endpoint also allows anonymous access. This way, an attacker can, for example, fake a remember-me token, assume the identity of the global system administrator and request non-public content from the search service without ever providing any proper authentication. This problem is fixed in Opencast 7.6 and Opencast 8.1
