TrustedHttpClientImpl.activate reads the global digest user and pass properties, and TrustedHttpClientImpl.execute unconditionally sets the X-Requested-Auth digest request header, propagates organization/user headers, and for GET or HEAD requests installs a digest CredentialsProvider with the global user and pass for any host handled by that client. This binds the advisory to source-backed mediapackage URL fetch, system TrustedHttpClient use, global digest credential configuration and transmission, and the production-source host-cache gating fix.

vulnerability.description: Open Access Management (OpenAM) is an access management solution that includes Authentication, SSO, Authorization, Federation, Entitlements and Web Services Security. OpenAM up to version 14.7.2 does not properly validate the signature of SAML responses received as part of the SAMLv1.x Single Sign-On process. Attackers can use this fact to impersonate any OpenAM user, including the administrator, by sending a specially crafted SAML response to the SAMLPOSTProfileServlet servlet. This problem has been patched in  OpenAM 14.7.3-SNAPSHOT and later. User unable to upgrade should comment servlet `SAMLPOSTProfileServlet` from their pom file. See the linked GHSA for details.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-27497 / GHSA-93qr-h8pr-4593 describes an OpenDJ denial of service where an LDAP search with alias dereferencing set to always against an alias loop can make the server stop responding to future LDAP requests. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 688a9ffc80d3c6c21c9cf1b89b1a6d8ed7d0cc1d, which is the direct parent of fix commit 08aee4724608e4a32baa3c7d7499ec913a275aaf. In that checkout, LocalBackendSearchOperation.processSearch checks dereference policies ALWAYS, FINDING_BASE, and IN_SEARCHING for subtree searches, loads the base entry, and if it is an alias directly replaces baseDN with baseEntry.getAliasedDN() and recursively calls processSearch. There is no set of already dereferenced DNs and no recursion guard, so two alias entries pointing to each other can cause unbounded recursive search processing. The pre-fix AliasTestCase covers normal alias dereferencing but does not include recursive alias entries. Fix commit 08aee4724608e4a32baa3c7d7499ec913a275aaf adds a dereferencingDNs HashSet, checks whether the next aliased DN has already been seen before recursion, removes the DN after recursive processing, catches StackOverflowError as an exception, and adds tests for recursive aliases and deep stack-overflow cases. This binds the advisory to source-backed LDAP alias dereference policy handling, unguarded baseDN recursion, missing recursion detection, and the production-source visited-DN fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-46096 describes a Solon v3.1.2 solon-faas-luffy directory traversal issue that can lead to XSS when attacker-controlled paths reach the Luffy file loader. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 4fdbc8f37e3e752d4b267b486116399597ea56b4, which is before fixed version v3.2.0 and before fix commit 49a3bf95fdcf050829843004b65a2b336ca6ddff. In that checkout, LuffyHandler.handle obtains the request path from ctx.pathNew() and passes it through handleDo to JtRun.fileGet. JtRun.fileGet delegates to the JtExecutorAdapter backed by JtFunctionLoaderManager, whose fileGet iterates registered JtFunctionLoader instances and calls each loader with the same path. JtFunctionLoaderFile.fileGet accepts the path without any ../ or ..\ rejection, calls fileBuildDo, and fileBuildDo constructs new File(_baseDir, path) directly. Because the default base directory is ./luffy/ and the pre-fix path is not normalized or constrained before new File(_baseDir, path), traversal segments can escape the intended Luffy repository and load arbitrary existing files as AFileModel content, which LuffyHandler then exposes to the executor path. Fix commit 49a3bf95fdcf050829843004b65a2b336ca6ddff adds an entry guard in JtFunctionLoaderFile.fileGet that returns null when path contains ../ or ..\, explicitly preventing traversal into or out of the repository. This binds the advisory to source-backed request path handling, unguarded external file loader path resolution, file content loading, and the production-source traversal guard added by the fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2020-13973 / GHSA-g8jj-899q-8x3j describes XSS in OWASP json-sanitizer before 1.2.1 when sanitized JSON is embedded in an HTML script element. In the reviewed exact source snapshot bb41f80ad575cb90ea6535976d7c17accb4b4c87, the class-level output contract says the sanitizer output avoids </script and ]]> for script/CDATA embedding, and sanitize(String) routes all input through sanitizeString(). The vulnerable sanitizeString() embedding logic only escapes the slash in </script-like substrings and escapes ]]>; it does not escape HTML parser state-changing sequences <script, <!--, or --> described by the advisory. PR #20 changes that same embedding block to operate on '<' and '>' characters, replacing '<' with \u003c for <!--, <script, and </script patterns and replacing '>' with \u003e for -->, and adds regression tests testHtmlParserStateChanges for <script, <!--, -->, and <!--<script>. These source spans bind the public XSS issue to the sanitizer entrypoint, documented HTML/script embedding contract, vulnerable incomplete embedding filter, and the output mutation helpers used by the fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-37422 / GHSA-h28c-453m-h9xm describes Payara before 5.2022.3 allowing path traversal for web applications deployed at the default ROOT context. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 7680990e55c04d628f16a591f950a2b3a4dcb401, which is the payara-server-5.2022.2 tag and is contained by fixed tag payara-server-5.2022.3. In that checkout, StandardContextValve.preInvoke obtains the request path, calls normalize, and blocks direct access only when the normalized path is null or starts with /META-INF/ or /WEB-INF/. The normalize routine handles leading double slashes, backslashes, /../ segments, and internal /./ segments, then prepends a leading slash if missing, but it does not collapse a path beginning with ./ before the restricted-resource prefix checks. As a result, a ROOT context request path such as ./WEB-INF/web.xml normalizes to /./WEB-INF/web.xml; that string neither starts with /WEB-INF/ nor equals /WEB-INF, so the restricted-resource check can be bypassed. The pre-fix StandardContextValveTest covers WEB-INF/web.xml and META-INF/MANIFEST.MF plus internal /./ normalization, but lacks leading ./ coverage. Fix commit 9f709cbe1c5546fe537754c257cb3122a6de38db, included in Payara 5.2022.3, adds explicit leading dot-slash normalization in StandardContextValve.normalize and adds a regression assertion that ./my.jsp normalizes to /my.jsp. This binds the advisory to source-backed ROOT-context restricted-resource path normalization, the leading ./ bypass, and the production-source fix.

In that checkout, StandardContextValve.preInvoke obtains the request path, calls normalize, and blocks direct access only when the normalized path is null or starts with /META-INF/ or /WEB-INF/. The normalize routine handles leading double slashes, backslashes, /../ segments, and internal /./ segments, then prepends a leading slash if missing, but it does not collapse a path beginning with ./ before the restricted-resource prefix checks. As a result, a ROOT context request path such as ./WEB-INF/web.xml normalizes to /./WEB-INF/web.xml; that string neither starts with /WEB-INF/ nor equals /WEB-INF, so the restricted-resource check can be bypassed. The pre-fix StandardContextValveTest covers WEB-INF/web.xml and META-INF/MANIFEST.MF plus internal /./ normalization, but lacks leading ./ coverage. Fix commit 9f709cbe1c5546fe537754c257cb3122a6de38db, included in Payara 5.2022.3, adds explicit leading dot-slash normalization in StandardContextValve.normalize and adds a regression assertion that ./my.jsp normalizes to /my.jsp. This binds the advisory to source-backed ROOT-context restricted-resource path normalization, the leading ./ bypass, and the production-source fix.

nodes.rationale: For a ROOT-context path like ./WEB-INF/web.xml, the pre-fix transformations do not match the internal /./ loop and then add a leading slash, yielding /./WEB-INF/web.xml instead of /WEB-INF/web.xml.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2016-9177 describes a directory traversal / arbitrary file read issue in Spark 2.5 static file serving, allowing remote attackers to read files via dot-dot URI traversal. The reviewed exact source snapshot ce57dfb949ed183405f75dee8cf3262b45c9b3b5 is the failed row's vulnerable 2.5.1 source snapshot. In that snapshot, MatcherFilter invokes StaticFilesConfiguration.consume before route matching. consumeWithFileResourceHandlers calls each ClassPathResourceHandler or ExternalResourceHandler with the servlet request; AbstractResourceHandler builds pathInContext from servletPath and pathInfo; the concrete handlers canonicalize URI path segments, append that path to the configured base resource, create ClassPathResource or ExternalResource, and return it if readable. StaticFilesConfiguration then streams resource.getInputStream() to the HTTP response. The 2.5.2 fix commit 26b57d0, titled Fix for #700 - Arbitrary File Read Vulnerability, adds DirectoryTraversal checks in both ClassPathResourceHandler and ExternalResourceHandler to ensure the resolved resource path still starts with the configured static-files folder before it can be served, and wraps consume() to log and reject traversal detection. This binds the public advisory, exact vulnerable checkout, source-backed static-file request-to-read path, and fix-bound base-prefix containment guard.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2018-9159 / GHSA-76qr-mmh8-cp8f affects spark-core before 2.7.2 and allows unintended static file reads through absolute or relative pathnames, file URL forms, or directory traversal sequences. The public fix commits for issue 981 harden ClassPathResource by rejecting WEB-INF/META-INF, URL-like paths, and cleaned paths that still contain ../; the first patch also rejected file: paths. In the reviewed 2.7.1 source snapshot, StaticFilesConfiguration consumes static-file requests, AbstractResourceHandler combines servletPath and pathInfo from the HTTP request, ClassPathResourceHandler canonicalizes and appends that path to the configured classpath base, ClassPathResource only cleans the path and then resolves it through the class loader, and DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstInClassPath relies only on a string prefix check after resource resolution. These source spans provide the reviewed classpath static-file traversal trace and recall anchors fixed in 2.7.2.

In the reviewed 2.7.1 source snapshot, StaticFilesConfiguration consumes static-file requests, AbstractResourceHandler combines servletPath and pathInfo from the HTTP request, ClassPathResourceHandler canonicalizes and appends that path to the configured classpath base, ClassPathResource only cleans the path and then resolves it through the class loader, and DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstInClassPath relies only on a string prefix check after resource resolution. These source spans provide the reviewed classpath static-file traversal trace and recall anchors fixed in 2.7.2.

nodes.rationale: The resource lookup path is built from request.getServletPath() and request.getPathInfo(), so attacker-controlled request path components flow into getResource(pathInContext).

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-47293 / GHSA-qpj9-qcwx-8jv2 describes PowSyBl Core XML Reader allowing XXE and SSRF before the v6.7.2 fix. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 72f79dec6d4292f892fbddd68a19c67935c7d81f. In that checkout, commons XmlReader memoizes XMLInputFactory.newInstance() and constructs XMLStreamReader directly from supplied input streams without disabling DTD or external entities. IIDM XMLImporter and CGMES NamespaceReader use the same default XMLInputFactory.newInstance pattern, while FullModel only disables ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD and ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA and still lacks the broader DTD, entity, and secure-processing controls added by the fix. Fix commit e6c7c4997ae8758b54a2f23ce1a499e25113acdc, titled Secure XMLReader by adding security properties and included in v6.7.2, centralizes XML factory creation in XmlUtil.getXMLInputFactory(), disables SUPPORT_DTD, IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES, IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES, external DTD/schema/stylesheet access, and enables secure processing; it also replaces the vulnerable reader call sites and adds XXE regression tests that verify secret file content is not leaked. This binds the advisory to source-backed XML parser construction, unsafe StAX defaults in shared readers/importers, and the production-source secure XML factory fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-47771 describes PowSyBl Core allowing deserialization of untrusted SparseMatrix data before the v6.7.2 fix. This binds the advisory to source-backed Java object deserialization in SparseMatrix.read and the production-source object filter fix.

The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout d6525f9e164338829058dfce187f0ff8af1f2790. In that checkout, multiple ReadOnlyDataSource implementations import java.util.regex.Pattern, compile the caller-supplied regex inside listNames(String regex), and apply p.matcher(name).matches() to filesystem names, in-memory names, resource names, tar entries, or zip entries. This binds the advisory to source-backed user-controlled regular expression evaluation over attacker-influenced or large DataSource name sets. The vulnerable snapshot has no re2j dependency and the listed DataSource implementations still use the backtracking JDK regex engine.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-48059 / GHSA-8qjw-9xgm-c9ff describes a polynomial Regular Expression Denial of Service in PowSyBl Core RegexCriterion before the v6.7.2 fix. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout e6c7c4997ae8758b54a2f23ce1a499e25113acdc. In that checkout, RegexCriterion stores a caller-provided regex string and filter(Identifiable, IdentifiableType) compiles it with java.util.regex.Pattern.compile(regex), then evaluates matcher(identifiable.getId()).find() against an Identifiable id. Criterion JSON deserialization accepts a regex field and constructs new RegexCriterion(regex), while the serializer emits the regex field for REGEX criteria. NetworkElementVisitor dispatches equipment criteria into Criterion.filter through doRespectCriterion, so repeated filtering over network elements can repeatedly evaluate the backtracking JDK regex over identifiers. Fix commit d8398f689a5ccd505bd62eee2bd6670a29133110, titled Fix potential polynomial ReDoS in RegexCriterion (GHSA-8qjw-9xgm-c9ff), replaces java.util.regex.Pattern with com.google.re2j.Pattern and adds RegexCriterionTest.polynomialRegexTest(), which runs RegexCriterion("(.*a){1000}") against a malicious Identifiable id "a".repeat(100) + "!" and asserts completion within five seconds. This binds the advisory to source-backed RegexCriterion regex compilation/evaluation over Identifiable ids and the production-source re2j fix.

evidence_refs.evidence: Old source returns scheme-qualified values unchanged, otherwise applies urlparse.urljoin(_request_uri(environ), value) without guarding value.startswith('//').
Patch guards network-path Location values with value.startswith('//'), rewrites them to /%2f..., and adds a no-open-redirect regression test.

nodes.rationale: The old WebOb Location header absolutizer treats URLs with an explicit scheme as already absolute, but sends schemeless network-path values through urlparse.urljoin. For a Location value beginning with //, urljoin can switch to the attacker-controlled authority. The patch guards value.startswith("//") and percent-encodes the second slash before urljoin. This is review-entry retrieval ground truth only and does not claim dynamic exploit proof.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-22227 / GHSA-4q2v-9p7v-3v22 describes Reactor Netty HTTP leaking credentials in specific chained redirect scenarios when the HTTP client is explicitly configured to follow redirects. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout a60f640c99d13af4e685c368a810c47b7f9fc628. In that checkout, HttpClient.followRedirect documents and configures redirect following while promising sensitive headers such as Cookie, Authorization, and Proxy-Authorization are removed from initialized redirect requests when redirecting to a different domain. HttpClientConnect.requestWithBody implements that cleanup when fromURI and toURI differ, but the redirect flow depends on HttpClientOperations sent-header/body state and redirect consumers being applied before headers are marked sent. The vulnerable HTTP/2 stream setup path creates and binds a new HttpClientOperations for HTTP/2 streams in HttpClientConfig.addStreamHandlers and H2 channel initialization without copying the parent HTTP/1.1 operations sent-header/body state. GHSA references fix commit 522892307ea89bf24fe634e8bfea35728c9bf411, which adds a copyState flag to HTTP/2 stream handler creation, copies hasSentBody/hasSentHeaders from the parent HttpClientOperations into the stream operations, and uses copyState=true for the HTTP/1.1-to-HTTP/2 upgrade stream while keeping normal HTTP/2 pooled streams false. This binds the advisory to source-backed redirect credential stripping, chained redirect signaling, and the missing HTTP/2 upgrade stream state inheritance fixed by the production commit.

In that checkout, HttpClient.followRedirect documents and configures redirect following while promising sensitive headers such as Cookie, Authorization, and Proxy-Authorization are removed from initialized redirect requests when redirecting to a different domain. HttpClientConnect.requestWithBody implements that cleanup when fromURI and toURI differ, but the redirect flow depends on HttpClientOperations sent-header/body state and redirect consumers being applied before headers are marked sent. The vulnerable HTTP/2 stream setup path creates and binds a new HttpClientOperations for HTTP/2 streams in HttpClientConfig.addStreamHandlers and H2 channel initialization without copying the parent HTTP/1.1 operations sent-header/body state. GHSA references fix commit 522892307ea89bf24fe634e8bfea35728c9bf411, which adds a copyState flag to HTTP/2 stream handler creation, copies hasSentBody/hasSentHeaders from the parent HttpClientOperations into the stream operations, and uses copyState=true for the HTTP/1.1-to-HTTP/2 upgrade stream while keeping normal HTTP/2 pooled streams false. This binds the advisory to source-backed redirect credential stripping, chained redirect signaling, and the missing HTTP/2 upgrade stream state inheritance fixed by the production commit.

nodes.rationale: Redirect request consumers and redirect BiConsumers are applied only before headers are marked sent, making correct sent-header state essential for whether redirect header mutation and cleanup are applied.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2018-1000129 affects Jolokia 1.3.7/1.4.0 HTTP servlet responses because the response MIME type can be controlled with the mimeType request parameter. In exact source snapshot 10727cab59a8fc2ae053bec6b2f26f48f1c4245c, AgentServlet.getMimeType reads pReq.getParameter(ConfigKey.MIME_TYPE.getKeyValue()) and returns that value directly when present. AgentServlet.sendResponse then calls setContentType with callback != null ? text/javascript : getMimeType(pReq), sets the status to OK, disables caching, and writes the JSON/JSONP response bytes to the servlet output stream. The GET and POST servlet request handlers pass the request parameter map into HttpRequestHandler, so externally supplied requests can carry both operation parameters and mimeType. The fixing commit 5895d5c137c335e6b473e9dcb9baf748851bbc5f removes the direct getMimeType helper, routes response type selection through MimeTypeUtil.getResponseMimeType, sanitizes request/default MIME values to only application/json or text/plain with invalid values falling back to text/plain, and validates JSONP callback names before handling the request.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-27136 / GHSA-G6WM-2V64-WQ36 describes an XML External Entity injection in LocalS3's CreateBucketConfiguration endpoint. In the exact vulnerable source snapshot 009901882be8b543e85b67c5ec2e9f30d83d62ef, LocalS3.createServiceFactory() constructs the service-wide XmlMapper from a WstxInputFactory that only disables namespace awareness; XmlUtils uses the same insecure WstxInputFactory pattern. CreateBucketController.handle() reads the request body through this XmlMapper into CreateBucketConfiguration, then stores createBucketConfig.getLocationConstraint() as the bucket region through BucketService.createBucket(). GetBucketLocationController later serializes the stored region in the bucket location response. The fixing commit d6ed756ceb30c1eb9d4263321ac683d734f8836f is explicitly titled 'fix XML External Entity (XXE) Injection (#172)' and adds XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false and XMLInputFactory.IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false to both LocalS3.createServiceFactory() and XmlUtils, directly disabling the vulnerable DTD/external-entity processing path.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-2240 / GHSA-gfh6-3pqw-x2j4 describes a SmallRye Fault Tolerance out-of-memory issue externally triggerable through metrics collection, where repeated creation of Guard or TypedGuard objects without an explicit description causes new metric objects to accumulate. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 8da7dae36f195608291687793ca9f12fd9567d93. In that checkout, Guard.Builder and TypedGuard.Builder document that a random UUID is used when no description is set, and the implementation initializes description with UUID.randomUUID().toString() in both GuardImpl.BuilderImpl and TypedGuardImpl.BuilderImpl. buildStrategy then creates a BasicMeteredOperationImpl using that description and wraps the strategy in DelegatingMetricsCollector whenever metrics are enabled. BasicMeteredOperationImpl.cacheKey() returns name, while DelegatingMetricsCollector and the concrete MicroProfile, Micrometer, OpenTelemetry, and compound metrics providers all cache MetricsCollector or MetricsRecorder instances by the operation or operation cache key. Therefore every newly created undescribed Guard or TypedGuard can introduce a fresh random metrics method tag/cache key that remains retained by the metrics maps, matching the advisory memory growth condition during repeated metrics endpoint access. Fix commit e8bcad3d5e8bbac0a3219bd5c13661adf6ed6bbb, titled fix memory leak in metrics, adds a descriptionSet flag, extends MeteredOperation with enabled(), passes descriptionSet into BasicMeteredOperationImpl, and changes DelegatingMetricsCollector to bypass metrics caching/emission when operation.enabled() is false. The fix message explicitly states that random UUID metric method tags were held in memory and that no metrics are emitted when no description is set.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-24789 / GHSA-7hpq-3g6w-pvhf describes a Snowflake JDBC Windows EXTERNALBROWSER authentication issue where the driver could open the browser through an untrusted search path; a local attacker with write access to a directory in %PATH% could escalate privileges to the user running the vulnerable JDBC driver. The local NVD/vulndb entry states the issue affects versions 3.2.3 through 3.21.0 on Windows and is fixed in 3.22.0, with patch URL commit 4f01bb8f9b708c71e7a2111c87371dbfc1d53dd6. The exact source snapshot 9e1a5acf12406b16c4780ca013f4c4db48b74b59 is a 3.21.1-SNAPSHOT checkout immediately before the SNOW-1708383 fix commit. In that vulnerable checkout, SessionUtil.newSession routes EXTERNALBROWSER authentication to SessionUtilExternalBrowser.authenticate(), authenticate obtains an SSO or console login URL and calls handlers.openBrowser(...), and DefaultAuthExternalBrowserHandlers.openBrowser validates the URL but, when AWT Desktop is unsupported, distinguishes only Mac from all other operating systems. Windows therefore falls into the generic else branch that executes a command string, runtime.exec("xdg-open " + ssoUrl), rather than invoking a Windows browser handler by a Windows-specific argument vector. The fixing commit imports java.awt.Desktop, checks Desktop.Action.BROWSE support, and adds a Windows-specific branch runtime.exec(new String[] {"rundll32", "url.dll,FileProtocolHandler", ssoUrl}); this is the source-level change corresponding to the untrusted-search-path advisory.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-24790 / GHSA-33g6-495w-v8j2 describes Snowflake JDBC temporary credential caching on Linux writing temporary credentials to a world-readable local file when EXTERNALBROWSER or USERNAME_PASSWORD_MFA authentication is used with temporary credential caching enabled. In the exact vulnerable source snapshot 3236d9840c61cdffa7093c631539523b9d1d6836, SessionUtil enables and uses CLIENT_STORE_TEMPORARY_CREDENTIAL to read cached ID tokens before a session and write returned ID/MFA tokens after login. On Linux, SecureStorageLinuxManager stores those credentials in temporary_credential.json via FileCacheManager. FileCacheManager builds ~/.cache/snowflake/temporary_credential.json and creates it with File.createNewFile(), then only logs/warns about broad permissions via FileUtil.logFileUsage; reads and writes likewise only log access and do not reject group/other readable files. Fix commit 9e1a5acf12406b16c4780ca013f4c4db48b74b59 creates cache files with POSIX OWNER_READ/OWNER_WRITE permissions on non-Windows systems, adds read/write/override permission checks, adds owner checks for reads, and adds FileCacheManagerTest cases that reject group/other readable, writable, or executable permissions.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-27496 / GHSA-q298-375f-5q63 describes Snowflake JDBC logging the client-side encryption master key of the target stage at DEBUG level during GET/PUT command execution. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout f8ab78a9567fcc3d3b245ba5a993110df9e3c6d8. In that checkout, SnowflakeFileTransferAgent.parseCommandInGS sends the GET/PUT command to GS, receives a JsonNode response, and immediately executes logger.debug("Response: {}", jsonNode.toString()). The same response is later parsed by parseCommand(), which reads data.encryptionMaterial through initEncryptionMaterial() / getEncryptionMaterial() and converts it into RemoteStoreFileEncryptionMaterial for upload and download flows. EncryptionProvider and GcmEncryptionProvider then consume encMat.getQueryStageMasterKey() as the key-encryption key for file encryption and decryption, confirming that the logged JSON field carries the sensitive client-side encryption material described by the advisory. The existing SecretDetector.maskSecrets() in the vulnerable checkout filtered access tokens, passwords, SAS tokens, AWS keys, and OAuth tokens, but did not filter encryptionMaterial JSON. Fix commit ef81582ce2f1dbc3c8794a696c94f4fe65fad507, titled SNOW-1660591 Remove sensitive encryption info when logging, imports SecretDetector in SnowflakeFileTransferAgent, changes the DEBUG response log to SecretDetector.maskSecrets(jsonNode.toString()), and adds SecretDetector.filterEncryptionMaterial() with a pattern for the encryptionMaterial object plus a regression test. This binds the advisory to source-backed GET/PUT response logging of encryption material and the production fix that masks the sensitive JSON before DEBUG logging.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2018-1260 / GHSA-rrpm-pj7p-7j9q describes remote code execution in Spring Security OAuth before fixed releases including 2.3.3.RELEASE. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 97e39dde7e88aae802be98de084a382886ca4255, which is the 2.3.2.RELEASE snapshot immediately before the 2.3.3.RELEASE fix line. In that checkout, AuthorizationEndpoint creates an AuthorizationRequest from user request parameters, stores it in the model, and forwards to the default user approval page. getUserApprovalPageResponse merges userApprovalHandler.getUserApprovalRequest into the model; DefaultUserApprovalHandler includes the original authorization request parameters. WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint then creates an approval-page template, injects the model/request scopes directly into SCOPE by string replacement without HTML escaping, and returns a ModelAndView backed by SpelView. SpelView masks literal ${ markers in its template, then PropertyPlaceholderHelper resolves placeholders by parsing each placeholder name with SpelExpressionParser and evaluating the expression against a StandardEvaluationContext over the model. This means a malicious scope such as ${T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)} can be introduced into the approval page template and evaluated as SpEL during rendering. Fix commit adb1e6d19c681f394c9513799b81b527b0cb007c, titled Remove SpelView in WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint and fixing gh-1340, deletes SpelView, rewrites WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint to build a static View that appends already-rendered content, escapes clientId, csrf fields, and scopes with HtmlUtils.htmlEscape, changes WhitelabelErrorEndpoint away from SpelView, and adds a regression test testApprovalPageWithSuspectScope using the payload ${T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec("cd ..")} to ensure the raw scope is not present and is escaped instead. This binds the advisory to source-backed SpEL evaluation of user-controlled approval-page content and the production fix that removes the SpEL renderer.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2020-5410 / GHSA-32xf-jwmv-9hf3 describes a directory traversal issue in Spring Cloud Config Server where a crafted URL can cause the server to return a resource outside the configured search locations. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 91843a9ddc7489275b679568bfce1e4c37af71e1, which is upstream tag v2.1.8.RELEASE and falls in the affected 2.1.0 through 2.1.8 range. In that checkout, ResourceController exposes wildcard resource endpoints, extracts the trailing request path from the servlet path, and passes it directly to ResourceRepository.findOne() for text and binary responses. The default ResourceRepository bean is GenericResourceRepository backed by a SearchPathLocator such as NativeEnvironmentRepository, whose getLocations() supplies file/classpath search locations. GenericResourceRepository.findOne() only rejects obvious invalid locations and paths through PathUtils, then resolves each user-controlled local path with resourceLoader.getResource(location).createRelative(local). If the resulting Resource exists and is readable, the old code returns it without checking that the resolved URL remains under the original location or any allowed search location. PathUtils in v2.1.8.RELEASE rejects WEB-INF/META-INF, URL-looking paths, and paths that still contain ../ after cleaning, but it has no post-resolution containment check for an absolute or encoded path that Resource.createRelative() resolves outside file:./. Fix commit 03eaadc25323d8c8c89f528e8585033ed90c50f6, titled Verifies resources are in allowed locations, is contained in v2.1.9.RELEASE. It first materializes allowed location Resources, changes GenericResourceRepository to call PathUtils.checkResource(file, location, locationResources) before returning a readable file, and adds PathUtils.isResourceUnderLocation() to require the resolved resource to be under the current or allowed locations. The regression test invalidPathEncodedSlash builds an encoded absolute path to src/test/resources/ssh/key while searchLocations is file:./ and expects NoSuchResourceException plus the new warning that the resource is neither under the current location nor under allowed locations. This binds the advisory to source-backed external resource resolution and the production containment fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-22965 / Spring4Shell describes unsafe data binding in Spring Framework where request-bound property paths can reach dangerous ClassLoader-related properties such as class.module.classLoader under specific servlet container and JDK conditions. In the reviewed exact source snapshot 925b07826067d57a8a057837a1b5973cb6fad186, DataBinder.bind() accepts PropertyValues, doBind() applies allowed/required filtering, and applyPropertyValues() sends all remaining values to the bean property accessor. BeanPropertyBindingResult creates a BeanWrapper for the target object, BeanWrapperImpl resolves local property handlers from CachedIntrospectionResults, and AbstractNestablePropertyAccessor recursively navigates nested property paths before setting values. CachedIntrospectionResults in 5.2.19 only filters classLoader and protectionDomain when the introspected beanClass is exactly Class.class, so it does not filter the class.module descriptor on Class nor ClassLoader-typed descriptors reached through module.classLoader. Public fix commit 996f701a1916d10202c1d0d281f06ab1f2e1117e / 5.2.20 changes this same descriptor filtering logic to allow only Class name variants and skip any descriptor whose property type is assignable to ClassLoader or ProtectionDomain. These reviewed source spans bind the external Spring4Shell issue to the DataBinder request-parameter binding flow, nested BeanWrapper traversal, descriptor exposure, and the fixed ClassLoader/ProtectionDomain filtering point.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-22233 / GHSA-4wp7-92pw-q264 describes a Spring Framework DataBinder case-sensitive match exception where CVE-2024-38820 lowercased disallowedFields patterns and request parameter names, but remaining cases could still bypass disallowedFields checks. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout f93132b11ef6aa5718d20a05846828659c082fe8, a 6.1.x commit between the affected 6.1.19 release and the fixed 6.1.20 release. GitHub compare shows f93132b11ef6aa5718d20a05846828659c082fe8 to v6.1.20 is ahead by two commits: edfcc6ffb188e4614ec9b212e3208b666981851c (Make use of PatternMatchUtils ignoreCase option) followed by the v6.1.20 release commit. In the exact checkout, DataBinder.setDisallowedFields canonicalizes each configured pattern and lowercases it with Locale.ROOT, while checkAllowedFields canonicalizes each incoming property name and calls isAllowed(field). isAllowed then evaluates allowed fields with PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch(allowed, field) and disallowed fields with PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch(disallowed, field.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)). PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch is a case-sensitive wildcard matcher whose direct equality, startsWith, endsWith, and substring scans operate with case-sensitive String methods. Therefore the DataBinder path still depends on lowercasing before a case-sensitive wildcard matcher, even though the same checkout already contains PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatchIgnoreCase() from commit 89ae20b9. If a disallowedFields rule requires real case-insensitive wildcard semantics that are not equivalent to lowercasing both sides before case-sensitive matching, the disallowed parameter can remain allowed and proceeds to applyPropertyValues(), where the request property values are written to the target object. Fix commit edfcc6ff removes Locale lowercasing from setDisallowedFields, updates the contract to say disallowed matching is case-insensitive, and changes isAllowed() to return !PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatchIgnoreCase(disallowed, field). This binds the advisory to source-backed DataBinder disallowedFields filtering and the production fix that uses the newly added ignore-case wildcard matcher for disallowed patterns.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-41234 / GHSA-6r3c-xf4w-jxjm describes a reflected file download issue when an application creates a Content-Disposition header with org.springframework.http.ContentDisposition, sets the filename through ContentDisposition.Builder#filename(String, Charset), uses a non-ASCII charset, derives the filename from unsanitized user input, and serves attacker-controlled downloaded content. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout e86dc9ad95204e71f93e1338cb7ccf379e3fbd70. GitHub compare shows this exact 6.2.x checkout is one commit before f0e7b42704e6b33958f242d91bd690d6ef7ada9c and two commits before v6.2.8, the OSS fixed release. In the exact checkout, Builder.filename(String, Charset) stores both user-provided filename and charset, build() passes them into ContentDisposition, and toString() emits a Content-Disposition header. For non-ASCII charsets, toString() appends a quoted filename parameter containing encodeQuotedPrintableFilename(filename, charset), then appends the RFC 5987 filename* parameter. encodeQuotedPrintableFilename iterates over filename bytes and copies any byte considered PRINTABLE directly into the RFC 2047 Q-encoded value. The vulnerable static PRINTABLE set includes all bytes 33 through 126 except '=', '?', and '_'; it does not exclude double quote (byte 34). Therefore a user-controlled filename beginning with a double quote and containing non-ASCII content can leave the quote unencoded inside the quoted filename parameter, matching the advisory's Content-Disposition reflected file download condition. ASCII filename(String) paths use encodeQuotedPairs(), which escapes quotes, and the exact checkout has tests for ASCII quote escaping, but lacks the UTF-8 quoted filename regression. Fix commit f0e7b42704e6b33958f242d91bd690d6ef7ada9c, titled Encode non-printable character in Content-Disposition parameter, changes ContentDisposition.PRINTABLE to set byte 34 false and adds a regression test formatWithUtf8FilenameWithQuotes expecting the quote to be encoded as =22 in the RFC 2047 filename and %22 in filename*. The related fd68ea6f commit applies the same fix on the other release line. This binds the advisory to source-backed ContentDisposition filename header formatting and the production fix that encodes double quote in non-ASCII filename parameters.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2011-2732 describes Spring Security header injection and HTTP response splitting in affected 2.0.0 through 2.0.6 and 3.0.0 through 3.0.5 releases. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout beb0ec4ba95265a7e3481b3eb8d87f3b922733ae, which is the peeled commit for tag 2.0.6.RELEASE and is in the affected 2.0.x range. The public advisory states that Spring Security allowed a request parameter named spring-security-redirect by default to determine the redirect target after login, and that the shared base functionality also affected logout handling so CRLF characters in a maliciously constructed logout URL could inject headers or split the response. In the exact checkout, TargetUrlResolverImpl defines DEFAULT_TARGET_PARAMETER as spring-security-redirect, reads currentRequest.getParameter(targetUrlParameter), URL-decodes it, and returns it as the target URL. AbstractProcessingFilter uses this resolver during successful authentication, then passes the resulting targetUrl to sendRedirect(), which delegates to RedirectUtils.sendRedirect(). RedirectUtils constructs finalUrl and calls response.sendRedirect(response.encodeRedirectURL(finalUrl)) without rejecting CR or LF. The logout path in LogoutFilter similarly derives a request-controlled target URL from the logoutSuccessUrl request parameter or other request-derived fallback and delegates to the same RedirectUtils.sendRedirect() helper. In the same checkout, DefaultHttpFirewall.getFirewalledResponse() returns the raw response, so there is no response wrapper guard against CR/LF in redirect locations. Fix commit f5fbda42e5f494f1a8aa96a0f8b35d60a4f57556, titled SEC-1790: Reject redirect locations containing CR or LF, changes DefaultHttpFirewall to wrap responses in FirewalledResponse and adds FirewalledResponse.sendRedirect(String) that throws IllegalArgumentException when the redirect location contains carriage return or line feed before delegating to the underlying response. This binds the advisory to source-backed request-controlled redirect target flow and the production fix that rejects CR/LF at the redirect response boundary.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-22223 / GHSA-hh3m-g4qj-4835 describes a Spring Security authorization bypass for method security annotations on parameterized types. The advisory states that Spring Security 6.4.0 through 6.4.3 can miss method security annotations placed on a parameterized superclass, interface, or overridden method when the concrete target method itself has no annotation, allowing the target method to be invoked without proper authorization. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 4993fa863a02008b606044cb897db6b54ec116f0, an affected 6.4.x source snapshot before fixed release 6.4.4. GitHub compare from this checkout to tag 6.4.4 shows fix commit dc2e1af2dab8ef81cd4edd25b56a2babeaab8cf9 as the first commit ahead. In the exact checkout, AuthorizationManagerBeforeMethodInterceptor.preAuthorize() installs PreAuthorizeAuthorizationManager for @PreAuthorize method security. During invocation, attemptAuthorization() calls authorizationManager.authorize(); if the result is null, the interceptor does not deny and proceeds with the method invocation. PreAuthorizeAuthorizationManager.check() obtains an ExpressionAttribute from PreAuthorizeExpressionAttributeRegistry and returns null when the registry reports ExpressionAttribute.NULL_ATTRIBUTE. The registry calls SecurityAnnotationScanners.requireUnique(PreAuthorize.class) and scans the invoked method plus target class. UniqueSecurityAnnotationScanner.findMethodAnnotations() delegates to findClosestMethodAnnotations(), but the vulnerable implementation locates overridden methods with targetClass.getDeclaredMethod(method.getName(), method.getParameterTypes()). For parameterized interfaces, superclasses, or generic overridden methods, the concrete method parameter types can differ from the generic declaration after type resolution, so getDeclaredMethod() can throw NoSuchMethodException and the scanner moves on without finding the inherited @PreAuthorize annotation. With no discovered annotation, requireUnique() returns null, the registry emits NULL_ATTRIBUTE, PreAuthorizeAuthorizationManager returns null, and the before-method interceptor treats the invocation as authorized. Fix commit dc2e1af2, titled Align Method Traversal with MergedAnnotations, replaces direct getDeclaredMethod() lookup with findMethod()/isOverride()/hasSameGenericTypeParameters() using ResolvableType and adds regression tests for annotations on parameterized interface, parameterized superclass, and parameterized method. This binds the advisory to source-backed method-security annotation traversal and the production fix that resolves generic override relationships.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-22228 describes Spring Security BCryptPasswordEncoder failing to enforce BCrypt's maximum effective password length. The Spring advisory states that BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches(CharSequence,String) incorrectly returns true for passwords larger than 72 characters as long as the first 72 characters are the same, affecting Spring Security 6.3.0 through 6.3.7 among other lines and fixed in 6.3.8. The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 36ea1b11a7dae7904e3c70b5e10fb01152fec5d4, which belongs to the affected 6.3.7 line. GitHub compare from this checkout to tag 6.3.8 shows fix commit 46f0dc6dfc8402cd556c598fdf2d31f9d46cdbf3, titled Enforce BCrypt password length, before the 6.3.8 release commit. In the exact checkout, BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches() accepts rawPassword, validates only null/empty/hash-format conditions, and delegates rawPassword.toString() plus the stored hash to BCrypt.checkpw(). BCrypt.checkpw(String,String) converts the full plaintext to UTF-8 bytes and calls hashpwforcheck(passwordb, hashed), which delegates to hashpw(passwordb, salt, true). The vulnerable hashpw(byte[], String, boolean) validates salt and rounds but has no check that passwordb.length is at most 72 bytes before it appends the minor-version NUL byte and invokes crypt_raw(). crypt_raw() feeds the password bytes into ekskey() and repeated key() expansion; BCrypt's algorithm has a 72-byte effective password limit, so two longer candidate passwords with identical first 72 bytes can hash equivalently against the same stored bcrypt hash. Fix commit 46f0dc6d adds an explicit passwordb.length > 72 IllegalArgumentException at the beginning of hashpw(byte[], String, boolean) and adds a regression test where 72 characters match but 73 characters throw. This binds the advisory to source-backed BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches password verification and the production fix that enforces the 72-byte limit before bcrypt hashing/checking.

The failed new-unified row uses exact source snapshot checkout 36ea1b11a7dae7904e3c70b5e10fb01152fec5d4, which belongs to the affected 6.3.7 line. GitHub compare from this checkout to tag 6.3.8 shows fix commit 46f0dc6dfc8402cd556c598fdf2d31f9d46cdbf3, titled Enforce BCrypt password length, before the 6.3.8 release commit. In the exact checkout, BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches() accepts rawPassword, validates only null/empty/hash-format conditions, and delegates rawPassword.toString() plus the stored hash to BCrypt.checkpw(). BCrypt.checkpw(String,String) converts the full plaintext to UTF-8 bytes and calls hashpwforcheck(passwordb, hashed), which delegates to hashpw(passwordb, salt, true). The vulnerable hashpw(byte[], String, boolean) validates salt and rounds but has no check that passwordb.length is at most 72 bytes before it appends the minor-version NUL byte and invokes crypt_raw(). crypt_raw() feeds the password bytes into ekskey() and repeated key() expansion; BCrypt's algorithm has a 72-byte effective password limit, so two longer candidate passwords with identical first 72 bytes can hash equivalently against the same stored bcrypt hash. Fix commit 46f0dc6d adds an explicit passwordb.length > 72 IllegalArgumentException at the beginning of hashpw(byte[], String, boolean) and adds a regression test where 72 characters match but 73 characters throw. This binds the advisory to source-backed BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches password verification and the production fix that enforces the 72-byte limit before bcrypt hashing/checking.

nodes.rationale: The byte-array check path also delegates directly to hashpwforcheck(passwordb, hashed), so the vulnerable length handling applies to both public checkpw overloads.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2018-1000850 describes a Retrofit 2.x before 2.5.0 directory/path traversal issue in RequestBuilder.addPathParameter/addPathParam where attacker-controlled encoded @Path values can manipulate the resolved relative URL for POST, PUT, or DELETE requests. In the reviewed exact source snapshot 7158698314daa138e993fac6a590ed19d78a8599, ServiceMethod parses interface @Path annotations into ParameterHandler.Path while preserving path.encoded(), and ServiceMethod.toCall() applies each handler to a RequestBuilder. ParameterHandler.Path converts the runtime argument and calls RequestBuilder.addPathParam(name, convertedValue, encoded). In 2.4.0 addPathParam directly replaces the URL template placeholder with canonicalizeForPath(value, encoded). canonicalizeForPath deliberately leaves slash and percent characters unencoded when encoded=true, so an attacker-supplied encoded path segment containing dot or dot-dot semantics can become part of the relative URL and is later resolved by baseUrl.resolve(relativeUrl) or baseUrl.newBuilder(relativeUrl). The 2.5.0 changelog explicitly records Prevent @Path values from participating in path-traversal, and the fixed 2.5.0 RequestBuilder adds PATH_TRAVERSAL detection plus a throw in the same addPathParam block after computing newRelativeUrl, including percent-encoded dot segments.

The M17 registry binds this case to zip4j 1.3.2 and the declared source repository iris-sast/zip4j, where tag 1.3.2 points to this checkout with commit message Add decompiled source for 1.3.2 (vulnerable) from zip4j-1.3.2-sources.jar. The upstream srikanth-lingala/zip4j repository does not expose this old 1.3.2 source snapshot, but the failed case already treats this exact source snapshot as its checkout; the reviewed evidence therefore uses source-backed spans from that exact checkout while preserving the normalized repo_key. In the exact checkout, ZipFile.extractAll validates only the destination folder and then passes all FileHeader entries to Unzip.extractAll(). ZipFile.extractFile delegates a selected FileHeader to FileHeader.extractFile(), which validates the output folder and calls Unzip.extractFile(). Unzip.initExtractFile() obtains fileHeader.getFileName(), ensures outPath has a trailing separator, and for directories constructs completePath = outPath + fileName and creates directories. For files, checkOutputDirectoryStructure() similarly sets fileName from fileHeader.getFileName() unless a caller-supplied newFileName overrides it, constructs compOutPath = outPath + fileName, and creates the parent directory. UnzipEngine.unzipFile() then opens getOutputStream(outPath, newFileName), copies zip entry bytes to that output stream, and applies attributes to new File(getOutputFileNameWithPath(outPath, newFileName)). The vulnerable 1.3.2 code does not canonicalize the combined output path or check that it remains under the canonical output directory, so a file header name containing ../ can cause writes outside the destination directory. The fixed 1.3.3 source snapshot 59aeea594ff885e06c25751dc6334dfea1bed8c6 adds a canonical containment check at the start of Unzip.initExtractFile(): it builds fileName and completePath, compares new File(completePath).getCanonicalPath() with new File(outPath).getCanonicalPath(), and throws ZipException when the entry escapes the target directory. This binds the advisory to source-backed archive extraction path construction and the fixed 1.3.3 containment check.

ZipFile.extractFile delegates a selected FileHeader to FileHeader.extractFile(), which validates the output folder and calls Unzip.extractFile(). Unzip.initExtractFile() obtains fileHeader.getFileName(), ensures outPath has a trailing separator, and for directories constructs completePath = outPath + fileName and creates directories. For files, checkOutputDirectoryStructure() similarly sets fileName from fileHeader.getFileName() unless a caller-supplied newFileName overrides it, constructs compOutPath = outPath + fileName, and creates the parent directory. UnzipEngine.unzipFile() then opens getOutputStream(outPath, newFileName), copies zip entry bytes to that output stream, and applies attributes to new File(getOutputFileNameWithPath(outPath, newFileName)). The vulnerable 1.3.2 code does not canonicalize the combined output path or check that it remains under the canonical output directory, so a file header name containing ../ can cause writes outside the destination directory. The fixed 1.3.3 source snapshot 59aeea594ff885e06c25751dc6334dfea1bed8c6 adds a canonical containment check at the start of Unzip.initExtractFile(): it builds fileName and completePath, compares new File(completePath).getCanonicalPath() with new File(outPath).getCanonicalPath(), and throws ZipException when the entry escapes the target directory. This binds the advisory to source-backed archive extraction path construction and the fixed 1.3.3 containment check.

nodes.rationale: UnzipEngine opens the output stream for the calculated output path, copies zip entry bytes to it, and applies file attributes to the resulting file.

vulnerability.description: Onedev is an open source, self-hosted Git Server with CI/CD and Kanban. In versions of Onedev prior to 7.3.0 unauthenticated users can take over a OneDev instance if there is no properly configured reverse proxy. The /git-prereceive-callback endpoint is used by the pre-receive git hook on the server to check for branch protections during a push event. It is only intended to be accessed from localhost, but the check relies on the X-Forwarded-For header. Invoking this endpoint leads to the execution of one of various git commands. The environment variables of this command execution can be controlled via query parameters. This allows attackers to write to arbitrary files, which can in turn lead to the execution of arbitrary code. Such an attack would be very hard to detect, which increases the potential impact even more. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this issue.

nodes.rationale: The old TYPO3 local URL sanitizer rejected only newline, carriage return, NUL, leading decoded whitespace, protocol-relative absolute paths, and a narrow set of relative-path characters before returning the original URL for redirect/header use. The patch replaces that partial invalid-character check with an RFC3986 character allow-list and adds regression cases for backslash variants, control characters, and unencoded spaces. provenance.rationale: CVE-2014-7816 describes Undertow 1.0.x before 1.0.17.Final, 1.1.x before 1.1.0.CR5, and 1.2.x before 1.2.0.Beta3 on Windows allowing arbitrary file reads through directory traversal in a resource URI. In the reviewed exact source snapshot 4aa98c80fa9962235c94f8666c30793d0018f95d, ResourceHandler.serveResource() directly passes exchange.getRelativePath() to resourceManager.getResource() and then serves the returned Resource; DefaultServlet.doGet() likewise takes getPath(req), only applies extension allow/deny checks, and calls resourceManager.getResource(path). CanonicalPathUtils.canonicalize() recognizes forward slash as the only path separator for dot-segment folding, so Windows backslash separators do not participate in canonicalization before resource lookup. ServletPathMatches.findWelcomeFile() also concatenates path plus welcome-file name and calls resourceManager.getResource() without rejecting Windows separators. The 1.0.17.Final fix commit ab8ba2adc9ca508dc22e41f1b63c34c5a78e80a1 is titled UNDERTOW-338 Fix tirectory traversal attack on windows; its diff adds PathSeparatorHandler to replace File.separatorChar with slash and canonicalize request, relative, and resolved paths on non-slash platforms, changes ResourceHandler to canonicalize relative paths and skip resource lookup when a non-slash separator remains, changes DefaultServlet to replace/canonicalize Windows separators and reject paths still containing File.separator, and changes ServletPathMatches.findWelcomeFile() to return null when a non-slash separator is present.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-48881 / GHSA-965r-9cg9-g42p describes missing authorization in valtimo-backend-libraries before 12.13.0.RELEASE: users who can reach object-management configured objects, or direct object URLs exposed elsewhere, can list, view, create, modify, or delete Objecten API objects without the intended object-level permissions. The reviewed vulnerable checkout is 33779f203273a6b02007217965d97d5036178d8e. The fix commit 6ab04b30d3dab816bfea32d40ba50e5dd4517272 has this exact checkout as its sole parent and is titled Added permission check for objecten api objects. In the vulnerable parent, ObjectManagementHttpSecurityConfigurer marks /api/v1/object/management/configuration/{id}/object GET and POST only as authenticated. ObjectManagementResource exposes those list/search endpoints. ObjectManagementFacade then delegates object read/list/create/update/delete operations to ObjectenApiPlugin, and ObjectenApiPlugin delegates all of those operations to ObjectenApiClient. In ObjectenApiClient at the vulnerable checkout, the constructor accepts only RestClient.Builder, OutboxService, and ObjectMapper, and each get/list/create/patch/update/delete method directly calls the remote Objecten API and emits outbox events without AuthorizationService.requirePermission or ObjectActionProvider checks. The fix adds an AuthorizationService dependency, objectenapi authorization enablement, ObjectActionProvider actions VIEW/VIEW_LIST/CREATE/MODIFY/DELETE, ObjectSpecificationFactory, PBAC permission configuration, and requirePermission calls in ObjectenApiClient for the affected methods. These source-backed spans therefore bind the missing authorization root cause to the exact vulnerable checkout and the corrective patch.

vulnerability.description: Vert.x STOMP is a vert.x implementation of the STOMP specification that provides a STOMP server and client. From versions 3.1.0 until 3.9.16 and 4.0.0 until 4.4.2, a Vert.x STOMP server processes client STOMP frames without checking that the client send an initial CONNECT frame replied with a successful CONNECTED frame. The client can subscribe to a destination or publish message without prior authentication. Any Vert.x STOMP server configured with an authentication handler is impacted. The issue is patched in Vert.x 3.9.16 and 4.4.2. There are no trivial workarounds.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2018-12542 describes a Vert.x Web StaticHandler path traversal issue on Windows: StaticHandler uses external request path input to construct a pathname intended to remain inside the configured web root, but vulnerable versions 3.0.0 through 3.5.3 do not neutralize backslash path-separator sequences that Windows treats as filesystem separators. In the reviewed exact source snapshot 3fe3873cc28b4d833c90f8989ff797a7b463da2c, StaticHandlerImpl.handle() decodes context.normalisedPath() and immediately calls Utils.removeDots(), whose implementation only treats forward slash as the path separator. The resulting path is passed to sendStatic(), getFile() concatenates webRoot with Utils.pathOffset(path, context), and the handler then checks existence/properties and eventually serves the computed file path through HttpServerResponse.sendFile(). The fixed 3.5.4 StaticHandlerImpl changes this same handle() path: after urlDecode(), when File.separatorChar is not forward slash, it replaces the platform separator with forward slash before calling Utils.removeDots(). That fix binds the public Windows separator traversal advisory to the vulnerable exact checkout, the StaticHandler request path source, insufficient separator normalization, webRoot path construction, and file serving sink.

nodes.rationale: The old Waku unstable_redirect helper accepts a caller-provided location and throws it as the redirect Location value while only documenting that pathname values are supported. The patch makes that contract executable by requiring a single leading slash, rejecting network-path locations beginning with //, and rejecting backslash or control-character variants before the redirect effect is emitted. This is review-entry retrieval ground truth only and does not claim dynamic exploit proof.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-23082 / GHSA-m9vj-44f3-78xw describes a path traversal flaw in io.whitesource:curekit before 1.1.4: FileSecurityUtils.isFileOutsideDir fails to sanitize/validate user-controlled paths correctly, allowing sibling paths such as /usr/foo-bar to be treated as inside /usr/foo. The failed new-unified row uses exact checkout 7b275a67a5992165deb186b2b3f7764ddd062d26, which is tag v1.1.3 and whose pom.xml declares io.whitesource:curekit version 1.1.3. In that checkout, FileSecurityUtils.isFileOutsideDir constructs File objects for filePath and baseDirPath, canonicalizes both as strings, and returns !file.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(baseDir.getCanonicalPath()). This canonical string prefix check lacks path-boundary semantics: an attacker-controlled file path that canonicalizes to a sibling path sharing the same prefix as the base directory can make startsWith(baseCanonical) return true, causing isFileOutsideDir to return false and incorrectly classify the outside path as inside the base directory. The v1.1.4 fix commit af35e870ed09411d2f1fae6db1b04598cd1a31b6 is the tag v1.1.4 commit and contains two patch hunks for this method: first adding a trailing separator to the base canonical path, then replacing String.startsWith with file.getCanonicalFile().toPath().startsWith(baseDir.getCanonicalFile().toPath()). The same fix adds a regression test with taintedInput /usr/foo/../foo-bar/bar and baseDir /usr/foo expecting isFileOutsideDir to return true. These spans bind the advisory to the exact vulnerable v1.1.3 source and the source-backed fix that restores path-component-aware containment validation.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2018-1047 / GHSA-fmr4-w67p-vh8x describes a path traversal information disclosure in org.wildfly:wildfly-undertow before 12.0.0, specifically through org.wildfly.extension.undertow.deployment.ServletResourceManager.getResource. The failed new-unified row uses exact checkout 4fd7bffaf2ee73201910684f2674aa1bced7fe81, the 11.0.0.Final source snapshot. In that checkout, ServletResourceManager.getResource first delegates to the deployment PathResourceManager. If that does not find a resource, it strips one leading slash from the request path and enters the servlet overlay branch. For each overlay it calls overlay.getChild(p) with the unsanitized path component and, when child.exists(), immediately returns a ServletResource backed by new VirtualFileResource(overlay.getPhysicalFile(), child, path). There is no CanonicalPathUtils.canonicalize(p) before overlay lookup and no child.getPathNameRelativeTo(overlay) containment check before returning the resource. WildFly PR #10748 / commit 9c0d5c7a2db8e78e3b600a3aae951e16aa7ae883 is titled WFLY-9620 ServletContext.getResourceAsStream, for deployments which have servlet overlays, serves files which are outside of the deployment. The patch imports CanonicalPathUtils, canonicalizes p before overlay.getChild(), passes the canonical path to VirtualFileResource, and wraps the return in child.getPathNameRelativeTo(overlay) so that an IllegalArgumentException prevents returning resources outside the overlay. These source-backed spans bind the advisory to the vulnerable overlay getResource path in the exact 11.0.0.Final checkout and to the production fix that adds canonicalization and overlay containment validation.

In that checkout, ServletResourceManager.getResource first delegates to the deployment PathResourceManager. If that does not find a resource, it strips one leading slash from the request path and enters the servlet overlay branch. For each overlay it calls overlay.getChild(p) with the unsanitized path component and, when child.exists(), immediately returns a ServletResource backed by new VirtualFileResource(overlay.getPhysicalFile(), child, path). There is no CanonicalPathUtils.canonicalize(p) before overlay lookup and no child.getPathNameRelativeTo(overlay) containment check before returning the resource. WildFly PR #10748 / commit 9c0d5c7a2db8e78e3b600a3aae951e16aa7ae883 is titled WFLY-9620 ServletContext.getResourceAsStream, for deployments which have servlet overlays, serves files which are outside of the deployment. The patch imports CanonicalPathUtils, canonicalizes p before overlay.getChild(), passes the canonical path to VirtualFileResource, and wraps the return in child.getPathNameRelativeTo(overlay) so that an IllegalArgumentException prevents returning resources outside the overlay. These source-backed spans bind the advisory to the vulnerable overlay getResource path in the exact 11.0.0.Final checkout and to the production fix that adds canonicalization and overlay containment validation.

nodes.rationale: For each overlay, the vulnerable code calls overlay.getChild(p) with the non-canonical path and returns a ServletResource if child.exists(), without checking that the child is still inside the overlay.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2025-23367 / GHSA-QR6X-62GQ-4CCP describes a WildFly Core RBAC access-control flaw where a user without write privileges, such as Monitor or Auditor, could suspend or resume the server because the suspend and resume operation handlers did not perform authorization checks. The original IRIS registry identity for this case refers to wildfly-core_CVE-2025-23367_27.0.0.Beta7, and the exact vulnerable checkout fef25f1036b0eee858261d892bfdca5fd86b0a50 is the WildFly Core 27.0.0.Beta7 tag. The same missing-check pattern remains in 27.0.0.Final, and the public advisory lists 27.0.1.Final as patched. In the vulnerable checkout, ServerRootResourceDefinition registers SUSPEND and RESUME operation handlers for running-server lifecycle operations. ServerSuspendHandler.execute acquires the controller lock, normalizes timeout, schedules a RUNTIME step, and directly calls suspendController.suspend(ServerSuspendController.Context.RUNNING) without calling context.authorize(...WRITE_RUNTIME). ServerResumeHandler.execute similarly schedules a RUNTIME step and directly calls suspendController.resume(...). The fixed 27.0.1.Final tag cd47c62e654de3b02f170c541870f2f09270309e imports Action and AuthorizationResult, calls context.authorize(operation, EnumSet.of(Action.ActionEffect.WRITE_RUNTIME)) inside both RUNTIME steps, and throws ControllerLogger.ACCESS_LOGGER.unauthorized(...) on DENY before changing server state. This binds the public RBAC advisory to exact source-backed suspend/resume handlers and the fixed authorization boundary.

evidence_refs.evidence: Old source performs remote image fetch/probe work without manual redirect rejection or an image allowlist/protocol boundary in the review-entry span.
Patch adds redirect: 'manual' and 3xx rejection for remote image fetches, enforces image remote allowlists for inferSize, and validates remote URL parse/protocol before probing.

nodes.rationale: The old Astro inferRemoteSize path streamed a caller-supplied URL through fetch without URL parse validation, protocol restriction, image domain/remotePattern allowlist enforcement, or manual redirect rejection. The patch adds those checks before and during the remote probe. This is review-entry retrieval ground truth only and does not claim dynamic exploit proof.

evidence_refs.evidence: Old source performs remote image fetch/probe work without manual redirect rejection or an image allowlist/protocol boundary in the review-entry span.
Patch adds redirect: 'manual' and 3xx rejection for remote image fetches, enforces image remote allowlists for inferSize, and validates remote URL parse/protocol before probing.

nodes.rationale: The old Astro remote image loader fetched an arbitrary remote image request with the default redirect-following behavior and no redirect rejection at the fetch boundary. The patch changes remote image load and revalidation fetches to redirect: 'manual' and rejects 3xx responses, closing the redirect-to-disallowed-target SSRF review-entry boundary. This is review-entry retrieval ground truth only and does not claim dynamic exploit proof.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2013-7285 / GHSA-F554-X222-WGF7 describes command execution during XStream unmarshalling before 1.4.7 when the security framework has not been initialized. The failed new-unified row uses exact checkout 768c6e417a75e7732fc591bee844e5e81af56a7d, which is tag XSTREAM_1_4_6 and whose pom.xml declares XStream 1.4.6. In this checkout, XStream.fromXML overloads directly create a HierarchicalStreamReader and call unmarshal() with the default mapper/converter chain. buildMapper() creates DefaultMapper, DynamicProxyMapper, aliasing mappers, and other mappers, but there is no SecurityMapper in the chain and no addPermission/allowTypes API. DefaultMapper.realClass resolves XML element or class attribute names into Java classes using the configured ClassLoader. DynamicProxyConverter.unmarshal reads interface names and a handler class attribute from XML, resolves both with mapper.realClass, builds a proxy, and calls context.convertAnother(proxy, handlerType). ReflectionConverter.canConvert(type) returns canAccess(type) for any accessible type, including java.beans.EventHandler in 1.4.6. AbstractReflectionConverter then instantiates and populates arbitrary objects during unmarshal. The 1.4.7 compare and release notes state that the release addresses CVE-2013-7285 arbitrary execution of commands when unmarshalling, adds a security framework to fine-control unmarshalled types, and makes java.beans.EventHandler no longer handled automatically. The security fix adds SecurityVulnerabilityTest with an XML dynamic-proxy handler class java.beans.EventHandler invoking a Run target and expecting XStreamException unless EventHandler is explicitly registered; it also changes ReflectionConverter.canConvert to reject EventHandler by default and adds the new SecurityMapper/TypePermission framework. These source-backed spans bind the vulnerable 1.4.6 unmarshalling path to arbitrary class/EventHandler instantiation and the 1.4.7 fix that blocks this dangerous type by default and adds type permissions.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2021-21345 describes remote command execution during XStream unmarshalling with the default out-of-box configuration through a manipulated java.util.PriorityQueue custom-serialization payload. The exact failed new-unified checkout f04bbec461f2c2a6f1e2cf41770f42c64aae24a4 is the peeled XSTREAM_1_4_15 tag and pom.xml declares XStream 1.4.15, which the XStream advisory states is affected until and including 1.4.15 unless callers explicitly configure a restrictive whitelist. In this checkout, XStream.fromXML creates hierarchical readers and calls unmarshal. The default mapper chain includes SecurityMapper, but setupSecurity grants AnyTypePermission.ANY and then applies a blacklist that only denies java.beans.EventHandler, java.lang.ProcessBuilder, javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter, jdk.nashorn.internal.objects.NativeString, lazy iterators, javax.crypto classes, and ReadAllStream$FileStream; it does not deny the CVE-2021-21345 payload classes such as sun.awt.datatransfer.DataTransferer$IndexOrderComparator, com.sun.corba.se.impl.activation.ServerTableEntry, JAX-WS iterator/accessor classes, or javax.activation.DataSource hierarchy. TreeMapConverter accepts a comparator child, resolves its XML class attribute with HierarchicalStreams.readClassType, and converts the comparator object. SerializableConverter handles custom serialization, resolves attacker-supplied class attributes through mapper.realClass, recursively converts field values, and invokes readObject through CustomObjectInputStream. The 1.4.16 compare/release adds CVE-2021-21345 documentation and extends XStream.setupSecurity with deny entries for ServerTableEntry, DataTransferer$IndexOrderComparator, JAX-WS iterator/accessor patterns, DataSource, Channel, BaseRowSet, and related gadget surfaces, binding the fix to the missing blacklist coverage in 1.4.15.

The exact failed new-unified checkout f04bbec461f2c2a6f1e2cf41770f42c64aae24a4 is the peeled XSTREAM_1_4_15 tag and pom.xml declares XStream 1.4.15, which the XStream advisory states is affected until and including 1.4.15 unless callers explicitly configure a restrictive whitelist. In this checkout, XStream.fromXML creates hierarchical readers and calls unmarshal. The default mapper chain includes SecurityMapper, but setupSecurity grants AnyTypePermission.ANY and then applies a blacklist that only denies java.beans.EventHandler, java.lang.ProcessBuilder, javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter, jdk.nashorn.internal.objects.NativeString, lazy iterators, javax.crypto classes, and ReadAllStream$FileStream; it does not deny the CVE-2021-21345 payload classes such as sun.awt.datatransfer.DataTransferer$IndexOrderComparator, com.sun.corba.se.impl.activation.ServerTableEntry, JAX-WS iterator/accessor classes, or javax.activation.DataSource hierarchy. TreeMapConverter accepts a comparator child, resolves its XML class attribute with HierarchicalStreams.readClassType, and converts the comparator object. SerializableConverter handles custom serialization, resolves attacker-supplied class attributes through mapper.realClass, recursively converts field values, and invokes readObject through CustomObjectInputStream. The 1.4.16 compare/release adds CVE-2021-21345 documentation and extends XStream.setupSecurity with deny entries for ServerTableEntry, DataTransferer$IndexOrderComparator, JAX-WS iterator/accessor patterns, DataSource, Channel, BaseRowSet, and related gadget surfaces, binding the fix to the missing blacklist coverage in 1.4.15.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-32697 is a sqlite-jdbc remote code execution vulnerability when the JDBC URL is attacker controlled. The GitHub advisory lists affected versions through 3.41.2.1 and points to release 3.41.2.2; that release includes fix commit edb4b8adc2447bc04e05b9b908195a4bc7926242, fix: use random UUID for external resources. In the reviewed 3.41.2.1 source snapshot, JDBC.createConnection() passes the attacker-controlled URL-derived address into SQLiteConnection, SQLiteConnection.open() accepts :resource: database names, resolves missing classpath resources as arbitrary URLs, and calls extractResource(). extractResource() writes non-file resources to java.io.tmpdir using a deterministic file name based on resourceAddr.hashCode(), reuses a pre-existing newer temp file, or deletes and replaces it before NativeDB opens the resulting file. The fix changes that deterministic temp file name to UUID.randomUUID(), confirming the source-backed vulnerable path.

The exact failed new-unified checkout 1874c4854f81d6af4a9471d3fe111cdbf713f336 is the v2.2.0 tag and pom.xml declares version 2.2.0. Upstream issue #2083 is titled v2.2.0 Add User Stored XSS vulnerabilities, Escape 20 length limit and gives a 20-character payload shape <script/src=//14.rs> that automatically triggers after being added. The user management page defines a username column bound to the server-provided username field, while the add form stricter alphanumeric validation exists only in client-side JavaScript and can be bypassed by posting directly to /user/add. These source-backed spans bind the stored payload entry point, persistence sink, and management-page recall surface for the stored XSS described by CVE-2020-29204.

vulnerability.description: XWiki OIDC has various tools to manipulate OpenID Connect protocol in XWiki. Prior to version 1.29.1, even if a wiki has an OpenID provider configured through its xwiki.properties, it is possible to provide a third party provider its details through request parameters. One can then bypass the XWiki authentication altogether by specifying its own provider through the oidc.endpoint.* request parameters (or by using an XWiki-based OpenID provider with oidc.xwikiprovider. With the same approach, one could also provide a specific group mapping through oidc.groups.mapping that would make his user automatically part of the XWikiAdminGroup. This issue has been patched, please upgrade to 1.29.1. There is no workaround, an upgrade of the authenticator is required.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2022-24897 / GHSA-cvx5-m8vg-vxgc describes XWiki Commons Velocity scripts not being properly sandboxed against Java File API read or write operations, patched in 12.6.7, 12.10.3, and 13.0RC1. The exact failed new-unified checkout 4f33e1efd74016fa9eb31b3c2fcd01bc6becd551 is the peeled xwiki-commons-12.6.6 tag and pom.xml declares xwiki-commons version 12.6.6, immediately before the 12.6.7 patch line. In this checkout, DefaultVelocityConfiguration installs SecureUberspector as the first default Velocity uberspector, and DefaultVelocityEngine initializes RuntimeInstance with those properties before evaluating templates. SecureUberspector constructs SecureIntrospector from configured bad classes and packages. SecureIntrospector only adds special allowlist handling for selected Class methods and otherwise delegates to SecureIntrospectorImpl.checkObjectExecutePermission; it has no File-specific allowlist or deny handling, leaving File write methods such as mkdir and renameTo outside the XWiki-specific sandbox policy. The 12.6.7 compare changes SecureIntrospector to import java.io.File, maintain per-class whitelistedMethods, add prepareWhiteListFile for selected safe File methods, and change checkObjectExecutePermission so File and subclasses are allowed only if the requested method is in that whitelist. The new SecureIntrospectorTest asserts File.toString is allowed while File.mkdir, File.renameTo, and CustomFile.mkdir are denied. These source-backed spans bind the vulnerable 12.6.6 Velocity sandbox behavior to the File API write access fixed in 12.6.7.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-29201 affects org.xwiki.commons:xwiki-commons-xml before 14.6-rc-1. The advisory states that restricted-mode HTML cleaning did not include an allowlist filter for HTML elements and attributes, allowing XSS and possible server-side code execution when privileged users viewed malicious content. The frozen registry's declared 14.6-rc-1 checkout 5d9632d9471f315052c76d7699a17414524ea093 is the patched release tag, so this reviewed-source row binds the case to the prepatch 14.5 release checkout bae1e23e73cafc007e5f28b39a04bfa0acf0199c. In the 14.5 xwiki-commons-xml source, HTMLCleanerConfiguration defines the restricted cleaning parameter, DefaultHTMLCleaner applies only control, body, list item, list, font, attribute, and link filters, and the component list contains no sanitizer component. In 14.6-rc-1, the XML module adds HTMLElementSanitizer, SecureHTMLElementSanitizer, HTML/SVG/MathML definitions, and SanitizerFilter. SanitizerFilter runs only when HTMLCleanerConfiguration.RESTRICTED is true, removing disallowed elements and attributes using HTMLElementSanitizer; SecureHTMLElementSanitizer implements element and attribute allowlists and rejects dangerous URI values such as script/data protocols unless explicitly allowed. These source spans bind the vulnerable prepatch absence of restricted-mode sanitizer enforcement to the 14.6-rc-1 fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-29528 / GHSA-x37v-36wv-6v6h describes the restricted mode of the XWiki Commons HTML cleaner allowing arbitrary HTML injection and XSS through invalid HTML comments, patched in XWiki 14.10. The exact failed new-unified checkout 7796f76096a3e94b7a0a96bf12b3b026922e3573 is the xwiki-commons-14.9-rc-1 source snapshot and pom.xml declares version 14.9-rc-1, which precedes the fixed 14.10 release. In this checkout, DefaultHTMLCleaner.clean parses user HTML with HtmlCleaner, serializes the TagNode, and then applies the configured filters, including the sanitizer filter from the default configuration. Restricted mode is documented by HTMLCleanerConfiguration.RESTRICTED and implemented in DefaultHTMLCleaner.getDefaultCleanerTransformations only by transforming script and style tags to pre tags. DefaultHTMLCleaner.getDefaultCleanerProperties sets parser flags such as ignore quest/exclamation and CDATA handling but does not omit comments in restricted mode. The test suite preserves comments in normal cleaning and the restricted-mode tests cover script/style transformation plus dangerous attributes/tags, but there is no restricted comment removal or invalid-comment test in 14.9-rc-1. SecureHTMLElementSanitizer filters elements and attributes after parsing, which leaves parser-level invalid comment handling outside the element/attribute allowlist path. The fixed xwiki-commons-14.10 tag 719ede2f8510fa69498761659de8d65eec5817db adds defaultProperties.setOmitComments(isRestricted(configuration)) with comments explaining parser-confusion risk, extracts isRestricted, and adds restrictedComments tests for ordinary comments and invalid comment forms starting with greater-than or hyphen. These source-backed spans bind the vulnerable prepatch restricted HTML cleaner behavior to the 14.10 comment-removal fix.
