vulnerability.description: XWiki Platform is a generic wiki platform offering runtime services for applications built on top of it. In affected versions any user with SCRIPT right can save a document with the right of the current user which allow accessing API requiring programming right if the current user has programming right. This has been patched in XWiki 13.0. Users are advised to update to resolve this issue. The only known workaround is to limit SCRIPT access.

vulnerability.description: XWiki Platform is a generic wiki platform offering runtime services for applications built on top of it. provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-32070 affects XWiki Rendering before 14.6-rc-1: XHTML/HTML rendering did not check dangerous attributes and attribute values, allowing XSS through attributes and link URLs supported by XWiki syntax. The frozen registry's declared 14.6-rc-1 checkout 48b2970c152accd0d9dbc461a2f04bb36686491e is the patched release tag, so this reviewed-source row binds the case to the prepatch 14.5 release checkout 9eae915967e41a40715caac41b1ad3464ef343b5. In the 14.5 xwiki-rendering-xml source, XHTMLWikiPrinter overrides printXMLElement and printXMLStartElement overloads only to handle whitespace, then directly delegates to XMLWikiPrinter with the caller-provided attributes. XMLWikiPrinter then adds those attributes to a DOM4J Element or forwards SAX Attributes directly to xmlWriter.startElement without any HTML element/attribute sanitizer. In 14.6-rc-1, XHTMLWikiPrinter imports HTMLElementSanitizer, stores an optional sanitizer, checks isElementAllowed before printing elements, and routes all attribute-bearing printXMLElement/printXMLStartElement overloads through cleanAttributes. The cleanAttributes methods call htmlElementSanitizer.isAttributeAllowed and translate disallowed attribute names with the data-xwiki-translated-attribute- prefix rather than rendering them as active attributes. These source spans bind the prepatch attribute passthrough behavior to the 14.6-rc-1 rendering sanitizer fix.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-37908 / GHSA-663w-2xp3-5739 describes XWiki Rendering XML/XHTML printing preserving invalid attributes by prefixing them with data-xwiki-translated-attribute- without further cleaning or validation, enabling arbitrary HTML injection. The advisory states this was patched in XWiki 14.10.4 and 15.0RC1 by removing characters not allowed in data attributes and then validating the cleaned attribute again. The exact failed new-unified checkout 0b0286c4caeab4cc1fdd617ec5bf0a91e6f46762 is the xwiki-rendering-14.10.3 release snapshot and pom.xml declares version 14.10.3, before the fix commit f4d5acac451dccaf276e69f0b49b72221eef5d2f. In this checkout, XHTMLWikiPrinter defines TRANSLATED_ATTRIBUTE_PREFIX as data-xwiki-translated-attribute-. The three cleanAttributes overloads for Map, String[][], and SAX Attributes each call htmlElementSanitizer.isAttributeAllowed on the original attribute; when the sanitizer rejects it, the code directly adds or returns TRANSLATED_ATTRIBUTE_PREFIX plus the original attribute name, with no removal of invalid data-attribute characters and no second sanitizer check on the generated translated attribute name. The prepatch XHTMLWikiPrinterTest only covers raw escaping and lacks parameter cleaning tests. The fix adds DATA_REPLACEMENT_PATTERN, removeInvalidDataAttributeCharacters, uses the cleaned translated name, and calls htmlElementSanitizer.isAttributeAllowed again before printing; it also adds testParameterCleaning cases showing in/valid becomes data-xwiki-translated-attribute-invalid and sanitizer checks both the original and expected translated name. These source-backed spans bind the vulnerable 14.10.3 translated-attribute printing behavior to the XRENDERING-697 fix.

The exact failed new-unified checkout 0b0286c4caeab4cc1fdd617ec5bf0a91e6f46762 is the xwiki-rendering-14.10.3 release snapshot and pom.xml declares version 14.10.3, before the fix commit f4d5acac451dccaf276e69f0b49b72221eef5d2f. In this checkout, XHTMLWikiPrinter defines TRANSLATED_ATTRIBUTE_PREFIX as data-xwiki-translated-attribute-. The three cleanAttributes overloads for Map, String[][], and SAX Attributes each call htmlElementSanitizer.isAttributeAllowed on the original attribute; when the sanitizer rejects it, the code directly adds or returns TRANSLATED_ATTRIBUTE_PREFIX plus the original attribute name, with no removal of invalid data-attribute characters and no second sanitizer check on the generated translated attribute name. The prepatch XHTMLWikiPrinterTest only covers raw escaping and lacks parameter cleaning tests. The fix adds DATA_REPLACEMENT_PATTERN, removeInvalidDataAttributeCharacters, uses the cleaned translated name, and calls htmlElementSanitizer.isAttributeAllowed again before printing; it also adds testParameterCleaning cases showing in/valid becomes data-xwiki-translated-attribute-invalid and sanitizer checks both the original and expected translated name. These source-backed spans bind the vulnerable 14.10.3 translated-attribute printing behavior to the XRENDERING-697 fix.

nodes.rationale: The parser-side translated-attribute mechanism removes the prefix later, making correctness of generated data-xwiki-translated-attribute-* names security-relevant.

provenance.rationale: CVE-2023-45277 describes Yamcs 5.8.6 storage API directory traversal in which the API can escape a filesystem bucket base directory and read arbitrary files. The exact failed new-unified checkout 9443a67d2aeda20fb73f68c5d571b515d68c05e4 is tag yamcs-5.8.6 and the root, yamcs-api, and yamcs-core POMs declare version 5.8.6. In this checkout, buckets.proto exposes GET /api/buckets/{instance}/{bucketName}/objects/{objectName*} and /api/storage/buckets/{bucketName}/objects/{objectName*}; the wildcard objectName is stored in GetObjectRequest.objectName. BucketsApi.getObject reads request.getObjectName(), resolves the bucket, then calls bucket.findObject(objName) and bucket.getObject(objName) without calling verifyObjectName or applying any path containment check at the HTTP layer. For filesystem buckets, FileSystemBucket stores a root Path, but findObject directly executes root.resolve(objectName), checks Files.exists, and reads attributes, while getObject directly executes root.resolve(objectName) and returns Files.readAllBytes(path). The only canonical containment check in the vulnerable snapshot appears in putObject, so read-side find/get can resolve traversal components outside root. The upstream source-backed fix commit b6db35e432e62fdff0447cf513369f0b8a848abf, titled 'Fix traversal vuln. on fs buckets. Reported by @visionspacetec', changes getObject, findObject, deleteObject, and putObject to call a common resolvePath helper, and resolvePath rejects paths whose canonical path does not start with the bucket root canonical path. These spans bind the CVE-2023-45277 arbitrary file-read behavior to the exact yamcs-5.8.6 source snapshot and the later filesystem-bucket traversal fix.

The exact failed new-unified checkout 9443a67d2aeda20fb73f68c5d571b515d68c05e4 is tag yamcs-5.8.6 and the root, yamcs-api, and yamcs-core POMs declare version 5.8.6. In this checkout, buckets.proto exposes DELETE /api/buckets/{instance}/{bucketName}/objects/{objectName*} and /api/storage/buckets/{bucketName}/objects/{objectName*}; the wildcard objectName is stored in DeleteObjectRequest.objectName. BucketsApi.deleteObject reads request.getObjectName(), resolves the bucket, calls bucket.findObject(objName), and then calls bucket.deleteObject(objName). The API does not call verifyObjectName on this delete path and has no path containment check. For filesystem buckets, FileSystemBucket stores a root Path, but findObject directly executes root.resolve(objectName) and checks attributes, while deleteObject directly executes root.resolve(objectName) followed by Files.delete(path). The only canonical containment check in the vulnerable snapshot appears in putObject, so delete-side find/delete can resolve traversal components outside root. The upstream source-backed fix commit b6db35e432e62fdff0447cf513369f0b8a848abf, titled 'Fix traversal vuln. on fs buckets. Reported by @visionspacetec', changes getObject, findObject, deleteObject, and putObject to call a common resolvePath helper, and resolvePath rejects paths whose canonical path does not start with the bucket root canonical path. These spans bind the CVE-2023-45278 arbitrary deletion behavior to the exact yamcs-5.8.6 source snapshot and the later filesystem-bucket traversal fix.
